body: Horton Plains National Park in Sri Lanka offers a scenic and refreshing outdoor experience, especially for those who enjoy hiking and being immersed in nature. We set out early in the morning and completed the trek to World’s End and Baker’s Falls, which provided great exercise in the crisp, brisk air. The landscape is beautiful, with sweeping views and a peaceful atmosphere that makes the hike enjoyable overall.That said, the experience did come with some drawbacks. The entrance fee for foreign visitors felt quite steep, and unfortunately, the facilities did not match the price being charged. The washrooms in particular were poorly maintained, which was disappointing. While it’s understandable that the park is located in a natural, remote setting, we have experienced far better facility standards in similarly remote locations—such as on safaris in Africa, where washrooms were kept immaculate despite being deep in nature.In summary, while the hike itself is rewarding and the scenery is worth seeing, the overall value for money could be improved with better upkeep of basic amenities.

body: Horton Plains National Park is one of Sri Lanka's most spectacular natural attractions, located in the central highlands at an elevation of 2,100-2,300 meters above sea level. This UNESCO World Heritage Site offers visitors a unique combination of cloud forests, grasslands, and dramatic cliff-edge views that make it an unforgettable destination for nature lovers and adventure seekers alike.What Makes Horton Plains SpecialWorld's EndThe park's most famous attraction is World's End, a sheer cliff with a 880-meter drop that offers breathtaking panoramic views. On clear mornings, you can see all the way to the southern coast of Sri Lanka. There's also a "Little World's End" with a 270-meter drop, equally impressive in its own right.Baker's FallsThis beautiful 20-meter waterfall is named after the British explorer Sir Samuel Baker. The cascading water surrounded by lush vegetation makes for a perfect photo opportunity and a peaceful rest stop during your hike.Unique BiodiversityThe park is home to endemic species found nowhere else on Earth, including the Sri Lankan samba r deer, purple-faced languor, and numerous bird species. The Montage grasslands and cloud forests create a mystical atmosphere that changes throughout the day.
title: Horton Plains National Park

body: Horton Plains National Park is unlike anywhere else I visited in Sri Lanka — high-altitude grasslands, cloud forests, waterfalls, and epic cliffside views all wrapped into one peaceful hike. If you're looking for a break from the heat and beaches, this is a fantastic escape into cool, fresh mountain air.We started the 9.5 km loop trail just after sunrise. The park opens at 6:00 AM, and I highly recommend getting there early. Not only do you beat the crowds, but you also have a better chance of catching clear skies before the mist rolls in over World’s End the highlight of the hike.The trail is mostly flat with a few rocky or muddy sections. It takes about 2.5 to 3 hours depending on your pace and how often you stop to admire the scenery. Along the way, you’ll pass through rolling plains, dense forest, and misty stretches that feel almost otherworldly. Wildlife is shy but present we saw sambars (large deer), plenty of birds, and lots of interesting plants.When you reach World’s End, the view is jaw-dropping a sheer cliff dropping almost 800 meters, with tea estates and distant hills stretching into the horizon. Mini World’s End comes a bit earlier on the trail and offers a similar, though less dramatic, viewpoint. After that, Baker’s Falls is a lovely place to stop, rest, and enjoy the sound of rushing water.Horton Plains isn’t about adrenaline it’s about quiet, natural beauty. It’s not crowded (especially early), and the air is cool and refreshing. You feel totally immersed in nature.
title: Misty Mornings, Stunning Views A Peaceful Escape into Sri Lanka’s Highlands

My Garmin fitness tracker recorded that we estimatedly climbed 42 flights of stairs uphill, and 51 flights of stairs downhill.While it is a beautiful place for a challenging hike, my poor review is because of the entry fees. Foreigners are charged around 40usd, which is about an exorbitant 150 times more than a local ticket. The 25usd price is misleading, because you also need to pay government taxes and service charges. There wasn't any indication of any services provided, or why we were charged for it.Toilets did not have much privacy. The road leading to the park was badly maintained, and full of pot holes. Man made trails were horrible and poorly maintained.
title: It is a nice location, with good views. However, tourists should not waste your money here, as you will pay 150 times the local

body: Honestly we had seen mixed reviews but are so glad we went and did the trail. Yes there is a pretty hefty cost, but it is a UNESCO site and you do get to walk through multiple environments. We had no issues at all at the ticket office, they were awesome. The trail is pretty easy to moderate - big tip - when you get to the start point there are two ways to go - go to the right, way less stairs and much better walk.
title: Do it !! It is beautiful!!

body: This is like no other part of Sri Lanka, if you start early be prepared to wear suitable clothing, it can get very cold. The landscape is unique and not dissimilar to New Zealand in appearance. It took my wife and I just over 3hrs to complete the full circuit and it’s reasonable difficult in many areas, not easy. If you do the circuit in a clockwise fashion it’s probably easier but make sure you wear decent footwear.
title: Great hike but be prepared.

body: Horton Plains in Nuwara Eliya is a must-visit gem. With breathtaking landscapes, thrilling hikes, and serene surroundings, it's an unforgettable experience. Don't miss World's End viewpoint and Baker's Falls. Pack your essentials and prepare for an adventure like no other! Highly recommend.
title: Unforgettable nature Beauty

body: We had an unforgettable experience exploring the breathtaking landscapes of Horton Plains in Sri Lanka. Every moment was filled with wonder. Highly recommend for anyone seeking adventure and natural beauty.
title: Unforgettable experience!

body: The park is new and obviously designed to make it easy for many people to see this part of Sri Lanka. There are a few things to know ahead of time. They are very serious about possible trash, so no containers of yogurt (as an example) are allowed in. They prefer reusable water bottles, but turned a blind eye (since we had no idea) though they did use a knife to remove all the labels from our hotel-provided plastic bottles). The trails themselves are wide and extremely well-groomed. Following the trails is easy (except at a very few crossroads). The system of marking the trails is not really complete yet. But the views are stunning - both the vistas, the overlook in the chasm called 'end of the world', and the close-ups while hiking in the forests.
title: A true touch of Sri Lankan nature.

body: Excellent Trip to Horton Plains. Fabulous 9k walk in a loop with great views and stunning scenery. Our guide helped us enjoy the day here.We stopped on the way up to watch the sunrise which was spectacular. Highly recommend a visit
title: Wonderful Place to Visit - Highly Recommend

body: It is definitely worth a half day tour and if you don’t want to be in a hurry, then maybe a full day to enjoy the scenic beauty,they say it rains nearly every day, it would be nice to have a good local guide to be able to explain to you the local details.
title: Awesome

body: Visiting Horton Plains in Sri Lanka offers a unique experience where the lush greenery and serene landscapes remind one of the Scottish Highlands or the Irish countryside. The highlight of the area is the 'World's End' - a spectacular viewpoint with breathtaking vistas. However, travelers should note that reaching this spot is quite a challenge.The path to World's End is not just a leisurely stroll; it involves navigating steep, uneven terrain with multiple climbs. It's essential to wear comfortable, sturdy shoes to tackle these paths. This trek might not be suitable for those with physical limitations, knee injuries, or families traveling with small children due to its demanding nature.Moreover, it's crucial to consider the weather before planning your visit. The rainy season can be particularly hazardous in this region, with risks of sudden floods. Therefore, it’s best to avoid monsoon periods for a safer and more enjoyable experience.In summary, Horton Plains offers a stunning natural escape for the active and adventurous traveler, but it requires good preparation and a consideration of physical abilities. It's a place that leaves you in awe of nature's beauty, but also reminds you of its demands
title: Word of Advise on visiting Horton Plains National Park Sri Lanka

body: This 9 kilometre hike starts with a smooth path and gets rougher. The scenery is beautiful like the Derbyshire Dales. It cost us 33,228 SRL (£82) to get in on 1st January 2024 for three visitors with a car and driver. Horton Plains has a small museum which is interesting. The toilets are not very nice and it has the dirtiest Canteen (Cafe) we saw in two weeks in Sri Lanka
title: 9 kilometre Hike

body: We were lucky with the weather for this hike. We left Nuwara Eliya at 5am to get to the ticket office for 6am. The hike is relatively easy if you are fit. Some awesome scenery and amazing views. Really glad we had the chance to do this hike. Would recommend!
title: 3 hour round hike.

body: Went to Horton place this morning. At 5 o'clock in the tuk tuk to drive an hour from Nuwara Eliya. We got there at 6am. There was already quite a line of drivers in front of the cash register, which opens at 6 am.The entrance fee was even more expensive than the $25. We had to pay 3290 rupees for the 3 of us and you also pay for the driver who can then drive to the starting point. That's another 5 km. We came across a group of deer. No further animals were seen in the area. I thought it was an exciting idea that the leopard is also walking around there. Apparently it doesn't attack humans ;-)At the starting point your bag will be opened and you will have to take out everything that is in the plastic. They offer paper bags. They take the labels off your water bottles. They were allowed inside.You can walk left and right. We went left and walked the more difficult route when you could choose. We didn't realize that at first and we wondered how all the 'oldies' were going to do this. You walk through very narrow, densely overgrown paths with an abyss next to you.Encountered 2 x toilets. Everything looks neat.It is quite a tough walk (9 km) with climbing and descending. Our legs were quite sore (also because we had only slept a few hours). It took us 3 hours.It is a completely different landscape than what you see elsewhere in the area.
title: Beautiful but expensive

body: Great 9km circular walk (about 2 hours and medium difficulty) in the clean and highly protected highlands of central Sri Lanka. We visited on a Sunday when many domestic tourists visit the park so it felt a little crowded and still we were lucky to see sambars (deers), black frog, bear-monkey, a giant squirrel (chipmunk) and a mongoose in same day. Awesome experience all in all.Recommendation: start before 10am when it starts to get really warm and a bit crowded.
title: Different nature of the highlands

body: We were visiting on a very cloudy day and we were very hesitant to do it because the mist that morning made the visibility bad. At the counter, the officer charged me 97.5 dollars without giving me proper explanation. When I asked to pay in rupees, the exchange rate he gave me was 10% lower than the previous day rate. Then i decided to pay in dollars but I asked him for explanation why im paying that much. First he said that I was paying for 2 adults and 2 kids. I corrected him that it was only one kid. Second he said that i have to pay for the driver and the car etc.. why should I pay for a driver licensed by the ministry of tourism only to drop me off. I felt he is ripping me off, trying to find explanation not to charge less than 97$I decided not to go. At the end, it is too expensive to pay almost 100$ for 10km hike on a misty day.
title: Beware of paying counter

body: I had an sunny afternoon trek through this park, the scenery is not like what we call plains in the US but more interesting. The rhododendron trees weren't blooming but the shape of them was unusual , a mix of a bonsai and an acacia. I took the trek from the visitor center through hills and a waterfall and then you see lakes then you will run into bakers falls. I didn't go to lands end , a lady said it wasn't worth it and the scenery wasn't much different, so I passed. If you have 2 days in nuwiyra eliya, visit here, but its about 30 miles away, but interesting scenery on the way to the park.
title: Unusual scenery

body: Unfortunately we had a very bad experience with Horton National park. Even all prices are written in dollars - they do not accept dollars or paying cards. Here is official price information in the Horton park ticket office:Entrance fee:One adult- 25$, one child between 6 and 12 years- 15$.Service charge:For one vehicle- 10$Vehicle fees:Cars- Rs 150Van/Jeep/Cab- Rs 300Bus/ Lorry- Rs 500VAT (above all charge) 15%There is no information about exact price in rupees or currency rates. So the currency rate can be any. Be careful of the ticket officer. The ticket officer calculated 32000 rupees for us 3. He asked if we have Srilankian driver. We said that no, we drove by ourselves, and he added 5000 rupees. What f.k! For what?! We did not have such an amount. Furthermore he tried to steal 5000 rupees from us. We gave him 30.000 rupees, after calculating he gave us 5000 rupees less. After some not very polite arguing he "accidentally" discovered that 1 banknote had fallen under his table We asked to pay in dollars or give us a discount or any advice, as we did not have enough rupees, the seller advised us to come tomorrow. We asked him to change some dollars to rupees but his price increased several times. We saw his colleagues- ticket controller and 2 other Horton park workers make fun of us but none of them even tried to help us. We decided not to beg him to let us enter the park anymore and drove away.I would recommend Park direction to train its workers to be polite with foreigners who pay such a big amount of money for entering the park and make ticket prices clear and exact.
title: Zero stars for staff

body: At 41€ per person (20times the locals) it's a legalized rip off. Had I not done 20km of a bumpy road on a bike, I would have gone back.And when I asked for a map, they told me I could take a photo of theirs
title: A legalized rip off

body: We did the early start- here around 6.30am., and as it was part of our tour, we didn't pay for it individually. It's quite a hike here- smooth paths one minute, rocky paths the next. I found it a bit hard, especially as the air is quite thin from the altitude- we couldn't chew our sandwich and breathe easily at the same time!But despite the effort we had to put in, it was SO worthwhile. Bakers Falls was lovely, and it wasn't crowded when we were there, so some lovely photos to take.World's End and Mini World's End have the most stunning view- it really feels like you're on top of the world.It's a real photo opportunity while hiking, so we really enjoyed it, despite the hard slog we had to put in!
title: Worth the effort.

body: The reservation is gorgeous don't miss. Entrance fee is $25!! 10 km walk through beautiful landscape
title: An amazing expensive experience

body: The trek of a lifetime. Have been trekking here since I was 2 years old, on my dad’s shoulders. Took my own kids this time, on the whole trek. What a beautiful ethereal place! Nature at its most divine…
title: Sublime

body: My friend and I visited in January 2023. Overall, I would recommend choosing antoher of the many attractions in the hill country over Horton Plains.Why go: it's a pretty and clean walk through a high-altitute plateau to a wide outlook down to the plains. We saw some deer in the open fields and interesting descriptions of the cloud forest. The walk is comparable in enjoyment to many temperate walks elsewhere. Easy to hire a return car trip from Nuwara Eliya (10,000 LKR). You can easily do the circular walk in 2-3hrw. Take sturdy shoes and a warm top layer. Start early: be at the park centre for 6:30am to get the best chance of the views before the clouds come in. If money is no question, then you will enjoy the park.Why skip: regretfully the park management seem to have taken to an extortion racket. A single person ticket for a foreigner will cost you around USD40 with the ticket price and the 'service charge', and even more if you actually want to pay in dollars (the clerk at the entrance will happily exchange to rupees for a hefty fee). That's probably about 40 times the price for locals. That is absurdly expensive for Sri Lankan standards and it's very expensive for what you get by Western standards, as it is just an unguided walk through the nature.
title: Foreigners skip. Pretty but a rip off

body: Got there just after 6.30am. Had an amazing walk round the trail with some stunning views at World's End and Bakers Falls, pretty much had the whole thing to ourselves... Get there early, we finished just before 9.30am. on the way back down the road it was a constant stream of cars coming up to the trail, so would imagine it's extremely busy the later you leave it.TipsGet there earlyWear comfortable walking shoes or trainers.Take your time, and listen to nature on the way round. body: Get ready for a walk, walk and walk for approximately 9.4 kms !! (Pheww)Undoubtedly this hike will give you a beautiful experience of walking in sweat, clouds, mist, rain and breeze ! One can experience all of them in the total hike !To consider for people who are not so adventurous and who prefer less walking. The plains may mislead you about the difficulty level !There are levels of walking and they are easy, difficult and more difficult!!And there are definitely the same the way they are listed. In the rains the rocks, the waking passage can be slippery making your hike really challenging. Till you reach bakers fall you will get an insight of your journey anyways !! One should be with very good quality hiking shoes with good grip which will be helpful while waking. Rain Coats, cap and some food stuffs are very important along with you. Remember to carry them in a paper bag as no plastics are allowed inside. They will remove the plastic covering of the water bottle too ( a good initiative though)Do try to start your journey maximum by 7:30 am to see a clear view near the world end ( if you fortunate). Else the clouds will cover you well and give another experience for photography only 🙃You will enjoy the named places called and mini worlds end and worlds end. They are the places where you can have a breathtaking views if there are no clouds.Be very careful of the steep elevation of the worlds end while doing some photography.This may take a minimum of 3 to 4 hours depending on the walking speed and time.Apart from this: undoubtedly this will give an amazing feeling once you finally see the finish gate 😎# leaving your foot prints behind 🙂# mythological: In the story, Hanuman set fire to Horton plains and that fire lasted for a long time. The original name, Maha Eliya Thenna carries the meaning, 'The hugely lighten ground'. Even now the upper layer of soil can be seem in a blackish grey colour. There had been some soil tests done by local universities, and it revealed that upper layer contains a high amount of Calcium Carbonate and Potash.
title: Not so plain for a walk, walk and walk experience!!

body: I really enjoyed Horton Plains, which included mainly a calm and moderate hike with just a few uphills to climb some short peaks. If your guide is taking you to the World's End and other items on the edge of the moutain, just know that climbing uphill means going thorugh some dense bushes and canopies, so wear something more comfortable than flip flops or flats. I loved the scenery and spotting birds and lizards sunning on the tops of the plants and shrubs. My friend did not enjoy it as much, as she was expecting much more. So I would place this site between a casual stroll through a meadow and a solid moutain hike

body: This is a beautiful hike --- it would be worthwhile to secure a guide who will know where to stop to view what will be the most AMAZING sunrise you will ever see. It simply took my breath away -- I compared the experience to Haleakula and this wins. After the sunrise we then proceeded into the park. We elected the clockwise path which is a bit shorter distance to the World's End which improves your chances of getting the view before the fogs set in. Although it did seem that even when there was fog, it was like weather at home: just wait a few minutes and it changes. The last 1/3 of the trail TO the World's End was so dense with shrubbery that without our guide I'm not sure we would have thought we were on the right path. For the number of people that take this experience, we thought it would have been more trodden, but it seems Mother Nature tries to keep it fairly dense. After viewing W/E, the remainder of the trail is a really nice nature walk. Keep your eyes out for green lizards that sit on top of the trees, little brown frogs that are fun to watch puff up with their croaking, and the variety of birds that inhabit the area. Unless you're familiar with how to spot these critters, this would be another benefit to befriending a guide.

body: We started our hike through Horton Plains early in the morning to catch a sunrise over the misty hills and terrains. What can I say, it was definitely worth waking up so early. We saw plenty of deers eating fresh grass even before we entered the main gate of the park, and then had an enjoyable walk along the route towards Baker's Falls. There are two options: you can start with the Falls and finish by the Little World's End or vice versa. We chose the first option and did not regret it. After we saw the sunrise, the sun quickly disappeared behind the clouds and we did not see it much until we reached the falls and the skies became blue. We took wonderful photos and had our packed breakfast right there on a bench, which was so romantic and enjoyable.When we continued our route towards the World's End, we realized how right we were in taking that path - we almost always hiked down rather than climbing up and it made our trekking way more comfortable and less tiring. The day before we hiked the Adam's Peak, so we could not feel our legs and feet after that and this path we chose turned out to be helpful :) Unfortunately, when we reached the World's End, a big cloud hung on top and covered all the view. We waited for 30 minutes and the situation remained the same. We still were pleased with the hike and the World's End because there was a certain mystery in this endless mist over the edge. You can literally feel you are on the edge of nowhere.P.S. In my opinion, you won't need a guide to hike Horton Plains. It is super easy and it is impossible to get lost on the way. There is literally only one path and it is a round journey, so whatever way you choose - you will end up in the same place. Only if a lady is solo and scared of being attacked or something??? But generally, for me it seemed peaceful and safe. And if a leopard comes out from a bush, I don't think that having a guide will be helpful right??)))Also the time you will spend there will be at least 4-5 hrs if you do not want to run along the whole route and wish to take nice pictures and just enjoy the nature around you. So don't listen to people who tell it is like a 3-hour hike. Maybe, if you don't complete the whole circle..)
title: Beautiful hike through the misty terrains

body: World's End ( Great World's End drop ) - is located within the Horton plains National park in Nuwara eliya. It is a sheer cliff with a drop of about 4000 feet ( 1200 m ). 01Km away from the main cliff is a smaller cliff with a 1000 feet ( 300 m ) colloquially known as ' Mini world's End '. The Indian Ocean 81 Km to the South can be observed on clear days . We advise to bring some weather clothes, rain coats and umbrellas as there are sudden rain . Totally around 11km walk from start place and to back. In side also you can visit to Baker's fall. Better you stay previous night at Nuwara eliya so you can start early in the morning . Light shoes & light clothes are ideal. Must visit place during your trip to Sri lanka .

body: This is a lovely trekking place with fresh air and beautiful scenery along the trekking paths. Some beautiful stops worth to check out are: 1. Little World’s End view point 2. Great World’s End view point 3. Baker’s Waterfalls We were so lucky to be able to see a wild Sambar Deer right in front of us up close before the starting point of the trek. Entrance fee is quite steep at LKR3,850 per person. Suggest to go early in the morning as we departed from our hotel at Nuwara Eliya at 5am. On the way up to Horton Plains, before reaching the ticket booth, we stopped at the roadside to watch the sunrise above the sea clouds. Horton Plains is a UNESCO World Heritage Site where is protected areas for its nature beauty. It is a plateau at 2100-2300 meters above sea level. Hence, be prepared for the warm clothing since it can be very chilly early in the morning. A complete route of hiking require at least half day time (4-5 hours depends on individual fitness level) and the trekking path is relatively easy for all age, but good walking shoes are necessary, plus adequate drinking water. Packing breakfast is advisable for people who do morning trek. Tight security check of the bag/ haversack at the entrance of trekking and no plastics allowed at the park. We were so glad that we did morning trek as the weather was cool and pleasant and completed our trek slightly before noon. Hence, most people do morning trek and be there early as there will be long queue for security check. An afternoon trekking would be warm and sweaty due to warmer weather in the day. We simply love this place and the beauty of Mother Nature!!!
title: Lovely Mother Nature!!!

body: I travel a fair bit. I'm used to long treks. I don't mind a tough walk. But...THIS WAS UNREAL!!!Once past the first, flat half mile or so you encounter much more difficult "paths". You literally have to haul yourself over boulder strewn pathways, watch for tree roots to trip over (I did fall), scramble down steep, smooth ravines with no foot holds, and do this for about 9km. To top it all someone up ahead of us upset a bees nest and we had to flee for safety. Unfortunately, 3 of our group got hospitalized with stings. The really disappointing thing is that the trek wasn't worth the effort. Other than the bees and a couple of deer at the starter hut we saw no wildlife at all. It was also misty so no view at World's End. With it having rained in the morning the stones were also very slippery. Other than seeing the waterfall it was a miserable time for me. Check the pictures for the sort of terrain you'll be covering. Unbelievable.
title: Difficult

title: Lovely park let down by dreadful cafe

body: Since it is really difficult to find anything concerning the exact cost of horton plains, I took a picture of our ticket. As you can see, we (2 foreigners, our driver & a tuktuk) paid 7534.08 LKR. Prices vary according to vehicle, from what I could tell. We also paid the tuktuk driver 3500 LKR to pick us up in Nuwara Eliya at 5am and return around noon. All in all, it's a very nice park with beautiful viewpoints and nice waterfalls - but it's also expensive (compared to sri lankan standards) and they should really add more ticket counters. We had to wait for half an hour in the freezing cold because many people wanted to get in early in the morning & there was only one counter! It's worth it to go early though, seeing the sunrise from horton plains was amazing.
title: Nice park - but expensive & many people

body: This really isnt worth the money. £34 for a couple to walk along a path and see 2 viewpoints and a waterfall. We thought the drive up to the park was more impressive. ..................
title: Nice but not worth £17 each

body: We were very lucky to have a totally clear day so could fully appreciate the magnificence of this place. The tracks are tricky in places so you need walking sandals or boots. We passed people in flip flops which is bonkers. Go early as the clouds build up and you would loose the spectacular views from Worlds End.
title: Busy but worth it

body: Must visit place .if it's not rain it's worth to visit . And 5 to 5 30 am start from nuware liay .One hour drive from nuware liay to Horton plains .The hiking will around 3 hrs .Worth
title: Best hike

body: Nice environment .Neat place .Beautiful nature .You can walk to the worlds end.Plz save the place
title: Good weather

body: This was a lovely National Park which is best seen in the early morning. We were greeted by some samba deer and wild boar. There is a 3 hour, 9 km walk. The path is up and down, rocks and steps which most ages can conquer. (I did!) The toilet facilities leave a lot to be desired however. There is a fee to enter the park and it would be beneficial if the fees paid could go to the upgrade of these toilets. Other than that set back it was a lovely place to go.
title: “Mini World’s end” and “World’s end “

body: Interesting part of the tour of our trip. We were advised to go very early having left our hotel at 5am, we were lucky that our hotel catered giving us a awesome breakfast pack. We were greeted with other tours lining up in the morning to get tickets, one word of advice is also to dress warm as in the morning it was VERY cold. The national park also restricts bringing in any food and you are checked at the entry point, it was strange however to see other tourists eating at the peak, i wasn't sure why our drink was confiscated. The hike was amazing, one of the best experiences ever, in the morning the hike was sublime, the pure calm and beautiful scenery was amazing, the best part was that luckily we had a good guide and was able to take a different route where we didn't see anyone. It felt like the whole park was ours, it was an amazing hike, to the peak the view was amazing and by the time we made it fortunately was much warmer. The hike wasn't too difficult and on the way back we saw bucket loads of tourists coming so it was another benefit to go when we did.
title: Highlight of my trip

body: You need to be here early to miss the build up of mist. We arrived around 06.50 and we certainly were not some of the first here. Despite what some people say, this is a pretty tough walk. I'm relatively fit but I'd still call it a challenging walk. My Fitbit recorded 17500 steps and 171 floors.I hate to tarnish an entire country but we were again inflicted to Chinese tourist hooligans. These moronic individuals who are only interested in taking posed selfies of themselves with 'V' fingers need to be taught how to be a tourist and respect others. We had seen it at religious sites where they run everywhere, shouting and pushing and completely disrespecting other people's religion. Today it was the utter disrespect of nature. Signs ask to be quiet, this is a place to take in the landscape, to listen to the wind. This is not a place to have Timberlake coming out of your I Phone at full blast As no one else was saying anything I'm afraid some Anglo Saxon words about their parentage was uttered and I guess they understood as they put their earphones on!!!!We were lucky to see the very rare bear monkey, an animal that is incredibly shy. Everyone around was hushed and we were able to see this amazing animal. Despite sushhhing and pointing to the monkey so they too could see it, these imbecilic people started to whistle at it like you would a dog. The monkey disappeared. At Worlds End again it was the Chinese that pushed to get the best vantage point to get selfies of themselves. China has just started tourism and this problem will only grow. Everyone appears aware of it but no one is teaching them that there are ways to be a respectable tourist. Our guide said this happens all the time. Perhaps responsible tourism behavior needs to be taught in school? The walk as mentioned is challenging, some good walking shoes should prevent slips. We saw people in flip flops. We also saw tourists with small children. This is not the place to take children. It is challenging enough on some of the steeper climbs, but looking after or carrying a child is an accident waiting to happen. It will be completely boring for them anyway and a pain for the parent.The drive from Nuwara is in the dark and therefore you don't see much, but coming back its a great drive and you see plenty of local life with good photo opportunities.
title: A nice walk spoilt by Chinese tourist hooligans

body: Horton Plains is an important area for nature and conservation this must be it's primary function and restrictions on where you can wander around are understandable. That said, the entrance fee of about £15 per person for what turned out to be a half day trip seems excessive. We arrived at opening time to see birds and didn't do the world's end walk, which is what most of the tourists were going for. I saw all of the species that I wanted to and was very pleased. The open air toilets were a great design and odour free. I hope the money spent goes to a good cause. In the UK national parks are free and most other countries that I've visited they only charge a nominal entrance fee. Sri Lanka could get a bad reputation for ripping off tourists. We've regularly come across one price for locals and a much larger one for foreigners. The recent implementation of free tourist visas for stays of less than one month is a great way of encouraging tourists to return after the Easter bombings. We came for two months and had to pay £160, we've spent a lot of money in that time. We'd consider returning but please reduce the visa fees.
title: Why so expensive?

body: amazing location beautiful view of sunrise many deer there lovely waterfall is very good clean location
title: amazing

body: Nice walk through the countryside. Track is sometimes slipery and muddy with tree roots, so do not go here in slippers. You can se here wild animals (deer, birds). If you wanna see the Worlds end. Definataly go there as soon as possible due to the clouds. Also in later time it should be overcrowded by other tourist.
title: Nice walk in countryside

body: This one is definately a case of fleece the tourist. Its a nice area, but there are equal places of note that are free or a lot cheaper.
title: Overpriced

body: A wonderful hike through bush and across plains to Baker's Falls - senstational, Little World's End and World's End.These last two offer spectacular views when there is a break form the swirling mist. Even the mist is amazing to watch as it swirls in and out. It is very peaceful and not at all crowded. It is hard to reach without a driver. The train stops 5 1/2 kms from the entrance and it is a hard walk. There were no tuk tuks or drivers waiting at the train to drive people. If you an get there, it is definitely worth the effort.
title: Fantastic hike

body: We were their early morning and i would suggest to everyone to wear layered clothes as in the early morning due to low clouds it will be chilly. Then you start the trek which approximately take 3 to 4 hrs depends on how much time you spend taking pictures and gaze to the lovely views. 2 main highlights which are the End of world (for landscaping views) and the Baker falls (waterfall). Worth the time for this trek i really recommend to go 👌
title: Amazing trek

body: This is my best national park to like visit again and again in every year. Every thing is very beautiful and windblown. I and my wife visited this national park last year.
title: Absorbed very clean fresh air from the hill country, Sri Lanka.

body: We were on a small group tour and the walk to World's End and Baker's Fall has been one of the highlights of our trip so far. You need to start early as otherwise the clouds roll in and you can't see the view. It's cold up there at that time of morning so take plenty of layers as later it gets really warm. I started with a down jacket over the top and ended up in a T shirt! Take hats and sunscreen too and sensible enclosed walking shoes. Quite rightly they don't allow any plastic containers in the park (other than water bottles with labels removed), so be prepared for a thorough bag check on arrival. I applaud this as there was almost no litter on the whole trek. There are toilets strategically placed throughout the park which I didn't use but others said they were fine. Would recommend this if you are reasonably fit. It's 9 kilometres and over quite slippery rocks at times so if you have agility problems you might struggle. I wouldn't want to do it in the rain but we had a beautiful day with great views from World's End.
title: Wonderful walk in beautiful countryside

body: We left at 5 a.m. and it took us 2 hours to reach the entrance to the National Park. There was already a long queue for tickets. It was quite cold then, and we were glad we had worn our jackets. At the entrance, they checked our bags for plastic. They even removed the plastic wrapping on the water bottles. That was impressive. It was a 7 km trek through various type of terrain. We saw a couple of deer grazing at the start of our trek. We took the route towards the right and were glad of having started early, as it was already beginning to get warm. Half way through we reached Baker's falls which was a wonderful sight. We continued on our way through rocky terrain at times and as we neared the point called World's End,we saw this amazing view of clouds coming down. We reached there and felt that we were literally among the clouds. We could not see anything below the cliff. The clouds were covering the view. After this point comes Little World's End and then the hike back is through shaded areas. Here you get to hear the sounds of different birds. Maybe if we had binoculars we would have been able to see them.
title: One of the highlights of our trip to Srilanka

body: This place was definitely worth the 5am start. We got there early and were leaving before it started to get very busy. It took us 2.5 hours to do the hike around, amazing scenery, wonderful views, loads of deer. Two toilet facilities on the way around which was great. Bring water, a light jacket and runners. Get there early or the clouds can come in quick and you won't see anything. Highly recommend!Medium level of fitness required.
title: Excellent

body: A hikers paradise with windy roads with different terrain. Bakers falls ,Worlds end are sights you need to let your eyes feast on,I wish they had marked `you are here' points with the amount of km's Make sure you start early morning to see the wild life
title: Go only if your fit enough to walk, The sights are amazing

body: Got in my hike for the new year. Woke up at 430 am to arrive at Horton Plains at 630 am. Got our tickets and started our hike around 715 am. Get a jacket as the early morning’s temperature dipped to 12 Celsius. The terrain is relatively easy and took us 3.5 hours to complete the full loop. At the fork road, we took the right route as our guide said it’s easier. Terrain started with rather flat land with brushes. Then the hike started downhill and the terrain became more trees with roots on the ground. We visited Bakers Falls first which is an amazing waterfall. Next stop is World’s End, which is the main reason to do Horton Plains. Amazing view and take a moment to take in the moment. The final stop was Little World’s End which is basically the same view but from a different point. The hike back is basically rocky and heading uphill. Highly recommended for avid hikers.
title: Amazing hike with great view and various terrain

body: Fabulous hike around waterfalls, Plains, jungle and ridiculous views. Takes about 2 hours from car park to car park taking in all the sights. Fully worth it!Tip - After giving your tickets in head right towards the waterfall first instead of left to worlds end. It’s a loop so you’ll see all of it. But so much quieter on the right. Enjoy!
title: Brilliant morning from Nuwara Eliya

body: 6 hours of leisure walk thru the Plains and enroute seeing sambars and squirrels and birds tweekings .. worth the hassle of getting up early in the morning And to top it all we saw mountain lions , while we were driving out the exit , trying to take picture of a sambar. See the picture to believe. Sambar took our attention to the lions in the backtround of our drame
title: Hiking of our lives

body: If you're a little lucky you can walk on your own and enjoy the amazing landscapes and maybe see some animals. But most likely you have to share the way with many other people speaking loud or even playing music from their cell phones.
title: Great landscape but too many visitors

body: We arrived just after watching the sunrise from a vantage point on road up to the park. Yes up and up and up. Roughly about £17 entrance fee.The 9km walk can be a bit challenging walking shoes helpful, though met young monk who was bare foot. Views are awe inspiring, and view points can be crowded, with many nationalities each with there own etiquette.You should get there early we arrived around 6.30amReason being you come for the views and wildlife, ad we left around 10.30 clouds were already beginning to drift towards the park.Also don't take plastic bags they are not allowed
title: Memorable views But get there early

body: We hired a driver from Nuwara Eliya to get here-- about 1 hour drive. It's a nice, easy, circular hike-- 9km in total and takes about 3 hours. Nice view point of World's End and Baker's Waterfall is beautiful. If you're lucky you'll see the purple faced monkey. Entrance is quite expensive, 3,650 rupee ($21).
title: Nice hike in the nature

body: Great place for a walk. I’m only giving it 3 stars due to the over priced entrances fees. $21usd to walk around is very expensive and is outrages. The views are amazing though
title: Over priced

body: Horton Plains Park is a nice hiking area. We enjoyed more than 10 km hiking towards the amazing water falls and coming back The weather was incredibly magnificent and unbelievable. The signage can be improved to reflect the height of each top to indicate to visitors the height from ground or sea level. Please note that the distance to the falls is not indicated all the way through and it’s only indicated at the beginning of the hike. Highly recommended and it will require an easy one full day to spend there.
title: “Nice place for Hiking”

body: If hiking is a must-do activity, go for it. If not, pass. 9 kilometers with moderate climbing and passing through rocks, the World's End offers a view that is way less spectacular than hiking trails in other places. It claims to house the most bird species within the country, but I saw a few only and the birds are mostly common in shape and small in size. The black-shouldered kite is interesting when it is hovering like a kite in the air.
title: Unspectacular hiking

body: This national park is absolutely beautiful. We visited early morning and it was cloudy and misty. It has a beautiful landscape covered with montane grassland, located in central highlands in Sri Lanka. There are a lot of flora and fauna that you can see them clearly if it is not misty. we got a guided walk and our guide was very knowledgeable about the area. we recommend to take this safari walk and expect to be wet.
title: Magical Natural Wonderland

body: Well worth the 5.30am start. We were even lucky with the rain stopping when we arrived and clear views at World's End. So lovely to walk through this beautiful national park which is well looked after and no plastic! Definitely recommend the walk up next to mini world's end which was a discovery - great views too. Didn't see any lizards or monkeys but saw sambar deer in the park area and leaving the park. Nice to have the plains to yourself for most of the loop.
title: So peaceful and beautiful

body: A lovely 9km adventure! However since it was pouring the day before- there was huge puddles that you could not avoid- so I recommend taking wellies on this hike. Worth the visit though. Lovely waterfall, however it was too foggy to view the world’s end.
title: Beautiful Park!

body: It is worth walking the distance just to witness the famous worlds end. The walk is about 3 miles, which is not yoo far and there is plenty to stop and see along the way.There are birds of different kinds everywhere, as well as plenty of animals, including the deer. We were lucky enough that one got very close on our way back to the car park!There is a very nice waterfall in Horton plains too, which is worth taking a small detour for. It was brilliant to be able to get so close to it. We could feel the water spraying on to us which was good in the heat of the day.Wobrlds end was spectacular. It really does look like what the words mean! The views were breathtaking. You could easily stay here and look out over everything for some time.There is also mini worlds end here which is very much the same but on a lower level. You go past this to get to, or return from worlds end. It to is worth admiring for a fair while.Definitely worth going to while here
title: Worlds end and a great walk

body: Magnificent views. You are up with the clouds. Water fall was great as a side walk. 2hr hike return for average person.
title: With the clouds

body: It was a pleasant walk through the cloud forest. Fortunately, It was not too crowded. We enjoyed the breathtaking view of the plains. We saw sambar deer at the plains. It was misty and cold. I would recommend to anyone visiting Nuwareliya to go there.
title: Great walk

body: Awesome walk with nice weather. We stayed the the plains green bungalow. Nayana the manager was kind enough to come with us on our track. His knowledge and love for nature made the visit even more wonderful.
title: Beautiful

body: I did the forest walk in the hills with a guide who recommended we leave Nuwara Eliya at 5:30am, so could start the walk at 6:30am. An early start means less likely to have mist & cloud. The guide recommended we go left at the initial branch in the track so more likely to see Worlds’ End views without cloud and then go to Baker Falls. Nice views down to valleys and lakes from the two viewing points. I should have read TripAdvisor first as then I would have packed the right shoes - I did the walk in sandals and coped ok with only a few slips, by being cautious, but it was rocky, slippery & muddy in places so would have been better in sneakers or hiking boots. The walk took me about 3 hours - the guide says it often takes 4 hours. I heard monkeys but didn’t see them. I did see a mongoose close up. Some sambar deer on the drive in & out.
title: Nice walk through forest, fewer animals than expected

body: The nature is great, the hike adequate for kids- not too hard and quiet interesting with monkeys and birds appearing here and there. But be prepared to pay 10 times the price for locals - for a family of 4 - 11K rupuies, which for a westerner is affordable but leaves with The Impression of having been cheated.
title: Be prepared to pay 10 times the price for locals

body: Gorgeous 8-9km hike. Unfortunately we started our hike too late so we got caught in a gigantic cloud which made some of the parts slippery and we couldn’t see ANYTHING of “world’s end”. Nonetheless it’s a gorgeous part of this world and shouldn’t be missed. It took us about 2 hours but then we didn’t hang around the sights too long and it wasn’t busy. Definitely start your hike at around 7AM!
title: Loved the walk through stunning scenery

body: We arrived on a warm but wet day but the place was not busy - it is not an easy walk and my fitbit said I did 13 kilometres and over a 100 floors - wet and slippery in some places and the terrain is very rocky in some places and quite difficult - wear proper walking shoes - Worlds End gives fantastic views and Bakers Falls spectacular - saw lots of birds/lizards etc and deer - this is truly the middle of the country and a wonderful way to spend an adventure date - VERY worthwhile - we were glad we had a guide
title: Wonderful long trek

body: We arrived by 630 and got dropped off at the main car park for Worlds End You will come to the point where the path splits, we went right as had read this way is much quieter and it's TRUE - it's like you have the whole place to yourself, we didn't really pass anyone until over half way as those that went left passed us! The paths are narrow and congestion slows you downThe difference to turning right is you go to bakers fall first, the other way you do little worlds end first, so another advantage to going right is that you see the vista from works end before the little one so you get the majesty first not the glimpse which I think could take the edge of worlds end if you saw that firstThe ground is quite uneven and if been damp or raining the clay soil is sloppySome of the walk requires some mild climbing - we had read it was a non challenging easy walk and I would debate that for those with poor knees etc - its misleading to say that. It's not rock climbing but there are definitely areas that require effort and thought The views are incredible Out of this world worth every stepWe are fairly fit and active and took us just under three hours There are about 3 loo stops on the loop which I was really impressed with
title: Stunning Scenery but More Challenging than you think

body: It was a tough six hours trek through the Plains. Plains could be misleading, as the tek involves quite a rocky terrain as well as slippery slopes. Would advise attempting this, when it is not raining and definitely with proper shoes.
title: Horton Plains

body: The hike itself is beautiful. If you go in oktober make sure to go early in the morning due to usual afternoon rains (this goes for any activity). Cause it's the lower season it's not too crowded with people.The tracks are mostly gravelly to rocky with plenty of muddy parts on the Plains part of the hike (world's end to Baker falls and back to the entrance). So bring decent shoes! It's doable on most type of shoes, but anything with good profile on them will give you a bit more traction and make the hike easier and more enjoyable.Keep your eyes open during the hike since there is plenty to see, mostly lizards, birds and deer, and if you are lucky monkeys or even a leopard (there was one near the entrance based on the behaviour of a few samba deer, but it never showed itself, probably due to the people in the area).
title: Beautiful hike, but bring the right shoes

body: Horton Plains National Park is one of the most beautiful natural places on Earth. It is a tranquil place highly recommended for honeymooners. We would love to visit this amazing place again!
title: Exploring the World Together

body: Super cool. Super mystery.You need to go there at 4 a.m, park opens at 6. You’ll see amazing sunrise on the road there.If clouds would be there, we think , it’s much more cooler. Because in sunny day you will see beautiful Mountain View. But in cloudy day you’ll see nothing. Absolutely nothing. Only the wall of clouds.And it’s unbelievable!Because this place is called The Worlds End. And if you want to see the end of the earth and to feel the infinity at the same time, you need to go there in a cloudy morning.You’ll feel something absolutely beyond belief.Must visit.You need to take something to eat/drink/warm clothes and snickers
title: Super.

body: Early morning walk to the end of the world .Conservation at it's best prior to admission onto the plains your requested to take nothing with you that could litter the area.Drink bottles allowed . You possessions will be checked.The walks are clearly mapped,we took the trail which firstly lead to Baker's falls well worth the walk themselves. Spotted many Leopard prints along the paths plus many different species of monkey,bird and insects. Arrived at the Worlds End to clear skies which provided uninterrupted views for miles,but within minutes the most rolled in obscuring the view. The walk itself is challenging in parts but with correct footwear it's fine.
title: Walk to the end of the world

body: My lovely wife and I took the morning hike through Horton Plains National Park to World's End. It's a hugely popular hike but in truth is rather unremarkable. The trail meanders through rather mundane scenery to the lookout point which offers pretty impressive views. Having said that, I wasn't entirely blown away by them. There are, for example, plenty of vistas in Scotland that are equally if not more impressive.The high numbers of visitors mean there isn't a great deal of wildlife to be seen. There were sambar deer hanging around near the car park, which I believe there often are, and we were lucky enough to spot a purple-faced leaf monkey while driving back to Nuwara Eliya. But don't expect too much. Leopard sightings around here are almost unheard of.All in all it was actually a pleasant enough hike. But the trouble is that it costs way too much for what it is. Entry fees for the two of us came to around 8,000 rupees (£35, $44, €40) which is just crazy. You'll also have to pay transport costs on top of that - for example we paid 3,000 rupees (£13, $17, €15) for a tuk tuk from Nuwara Eliya. And it simply isn't worth the money for what it is.
title: Unremarkable hike, excessive admission fees... just not worth it

body: The Horton Plains National Park is definitely worth it. The “end of the world” provides a stunning view over the valley. The 9km itinerary is very enjoyable and spectacular. The waterfalls also are quite beautiful even tough in Sri Lanka there are much better ones. The only thing that was very annoying is that as a “foreigner” you will be charged 4000/5000 rs.
title: Beautiful place

body: The place is beautiful, with a few hidden gems around, worthwhile. But we felt that the entrance ticket was a bit overpriced.
title: Pretty, but overpriced

body: Hortan plains is a plateau set on high mountains of Sri Lanka. It sits at a height of more than 2000 meters above sea level. This plateau spreads over 3150 hectares, and is a great attraction to both local and foreign tourists. It can be reached by motorable road from Pattipola or Ohiya. When you climb from below you can see how vegetation differs and weather becomes colder.When you enter the plateau you see it’s covered with mist and stunted trees due to the strong winds on the plains. Also you can find small ponds of water with water lilies. As you go further the trees become fewer but instead there are low growing bushes and more of a moor type of vegetation.Main attraction in Hortan plains is ‘Worlds End, a 700 meter breathtaking sheer drop. This drop has the most magnificent view of the sourthern wall of central highlands.Another attraction is Baker’s falls. It can be reached after a long walk through the forest. The plains are home for leopards,elk, monkeys and jackals. Plain is also home for many endemic plants.When you make a visit please make sure you do not harm the plants and animals and you will only observe the beauty of it. Worth making a trip.
title: Horton Plains

body: World’s End was an anticlimax, and we had good weather there. It is a good 9 km walk with varied terrain, scenery and views but nothing special compared with many walks in the UK’s National Parks and elsewhere in the world. Not worth the early start and high fees and getting there is not simple. We were travelling from Nuwara Eliya to Ella, so did the World’s End walk on the way. We hired a car and driver for LRK10,000. The Horton Plains NP fee for two people, plus the car and driver was LKR8,100. Apart from the first kilometre or so there is no sign of the money raised from foreign tourists being used to maintain the route. In places the path would become a watercourse after rain, luckily it was dry when we were there. I have no problem with foreigners being charged more than locals but the price charged should be reasonable and it would be good to see the money generated being invested in the site.
title: Nothing special compared to National Parks elsewhere in the world and expensive

body: The most beautiful hike we had in Sri Lanka. Worthy to go early on the morning, and worthy even without the view - often foggy.No leeches :)
title: Nice hike

body: The hike through the park took us through several micro climates and some very scenic areas. The trail Is a bit rough in places especially during the wet. When we hiked, it was more like a shallow creek in places. I read other reviews complaining about not seeing any deer, though I am not surprised as most walkers are quite noisy and would scare most animals away from the trails. World's End was enveloped in cloud the day we hiked there, so no spectacular views, but a lovely place to rest anyway. The falls are worth the walk in as well.
title: Cloud forest

body: We should have heeded those who advised against doing this walk, particularly agree with all that Aaron and other gentleman below has said on this site. It’s a lot of money to get in, an hours drive to get there, and in fact we only saw deer outside the park.Guess it depends where you are from but we felt we could be doing a walk in one of our National Parks that is just as beautiful and free to all. SL needs to seriously rethink about some of these out of proportion fees for foreign visitors if they want to build tourism numbers.
title: Wish we hadn’t bothered...

body: We did the walk along Horton Plains to see Worlds end and bakers falls . It is worth getting there when the park opens at 6am as the walk can take a while and the clouds come in during the day. Wear sensible shoes as some of the walk is along a rocky path and it is not easy to walk along. You can see deer and lots of birds Well worth a visit
title: Horton plains

body: It was a very cool and windy place ! Required to bring wind breaker for the trek. Nice trekking. Nice scenery at the “world end”. Suggest to bring breakfast box and have it when you arrive at “world end” view point and continue to trek for waterfall.
title: Wonderful scenery !

body: Not one to write many reviews, but felt I had to warn fellow travellers about this one. Honestly there really isn't anything special about this place in consideration to any other places I've been. It would be worth it if you had time and it was free I guess.... But to be charged 8000 odd rupees for me and my friend is a disgrace, clear exploitation of tourists good will, and I would consider that you don't pay it and encourage this greedy behaviour.
title: Ridiculously overpriced (Avoid at all costs)

body: 40euro for 2 persons is way to expensive for this.It is just a normal hike, Worlds end could be nice if your lucky, we had only clouds...I don't get where all this money goes to.There is only few staff at entrance and a worthless museum.No wildlife to be seen. Only saw some deer outside the national park area.....Better hiking to do in Ella for free.
title: Overpriced hike

body: Wear comfy clothing and be prepared for rain! This place is a great place to walk, we walked up to World's End with it's amazing views and then around to Baker's Falls. Such a beautiful waterfall. This is an amazing part of Sri Lanka, the climate here is so different from the rest of the country. I can see why they call it Little England! We only saw some deer but still enjoyed the day and the fresh air.
title: Great views!

body: Youcan experience a different type of climate up there with different flora and fauna compared to other places in the coutry. World's end drop is just one thing visit within this amazing area.
title: One of the most awesome places in Sri Lanka

body: we arrived early morning to avoid the afternoon mist. we had to walk about 01 to 02 km from the entrance to get to the famous viewpoint where you could see an entire town from the top. it is advisable to stay of the edge of the cliff and avoid having any accidents as many people have fallen off this cliff.
title: deer spotting at horton plains

body: I went with my family via haputale boralanda ,ohiya to Horton plains. It's a lovely drive through the green scenery with gloomy weather and cool I really enjoyed driving its took one and half hours to reach on the way we saw jungle fowl and birds. We reached by 8.30 am and went inside the park it's a 9 km walk it's a lovely experience you we had. The breathing take views is amazing you have to visit this place if you are a Sri lanka . I would recommend to foreigners too.
title: Lovely cool place to be

body: the best hiking experience in sri lanka. we visited nuwara eliya and then took the hike the day after. we started off early morning and it was amazing. we were able to spot deer, a leopard and migrating birds. wonderful experience.
title: Memorable Hike to the top

body: We were in Nuwara Eliya, Small England of Sri Lanka (elevation 2000+ meters above sea level, average temp 12 degrees). We Started our trip early morning at 5.00 am which will take around 1 hour due to foggy road.It is 30 kms south of Nuwara Eliya lies the famous Horton Plains (2,100 m) sorrounded by mountain ranges.It starts about 400 meters from the Entrance Gate. Start off early and aim to get there before 6.30am for the best views over World's End, before the mist & cloud cover the area. Take the route that goes to mini World's End first from left. The hike takes about 3 to 4 hours, do not forget to bring water, snack, umbrella (in case if it rains) and wear proper hiking shoes. You will first reach to Mini World's End ( 2 Kms from Entrance). From Mini worlds Ends to Greater World's End is further 3 Kms. Further to reach Baker's Falls you need to Walk 2 Kms. On the way you will get a Public Toilet which is not very clean & hygienic with no water tap in it. Returning back to gate you will get to see Chimney Pool (1.5 Kms from Greater World's End.And at last to reach the Gate its 2 Kms In rain get muddy and slippery, especially when you go towards Baker's Falls. There is only one toilet in entire route inside the Park, so try to use one before you leave your hotel, or else at the entrance of the national park, there is a toilet.Ticket price is well worth it. Grassland plains, mangrove forests.There is a restaurant outside the gate were you can refresh yourself .We paid LKR 7,950.00 for 2 person incl all. for the entrance ticket.
title: A Trip we can never forget

body: You need to set off early in the day to avoid the noonday sun and also find a parking space in this popular national park. The views are stunning but if you suffer from vertigo, I would give this a miss. Ground is quite uneven so ware good quality walking boots and be prepared for a workout!
title: High plains drifter

body: Park is easily accessible from Nuwara Eliya, you can choose from different kind of transports. On the way back you can also visit dairy firms.Park is one of the most pristine and serene natural parks i have visited till now. Took the worlds end and & bakers fall trek,which is about 9km hiking. Surprisingly they have well maintained washroom facilities inside the park too.Tips would be bring raincoats and a spare pair of cloths.
title: One of the most fulfilling experience!

body: This has so far been the unexpected highlight of our holiday. Just under 3 hours of trekking on pretty rugged terrain (definitely not suitable for flip flops) but the views were beyond amazing! I don’t think any photo would do it justice ... A 5:30am start, 23,000 steps and 196 floors climbed according to my Fitbit made for a busy morning!
title: Wow!!! Just wow!!!

body: Awesome. We stayed at a lodge named Country Lodge which is in Nuwara Eliya. From the lodge we took a vehicle and started the journey at 5:30 in the morning. It was a brilliant experience exploring this scenic wildlife. Make sure you be there early as possible.
title: A fulfilled experience

body: Most serene and pristine natural park, and the one and only where a visitor can walk and see the wonders of the nature. You can see the "World's End"- a 1000 ft cliff and the "Baker's Falls " in one full visit. The flora and fauna is so unique where you will not see any such combination anywhere. Some species are endemic only to this wildlife park. A must go for any nature lover. Two wildlife bungalows, and a few camping sites available - can be booked at the Wildlife Dpt. Mahaeliya Bungalow is highly recommended - where wildlife if 24X7 at the doorsteps - Sambar and Jungle Fowl (the national bird in Sri Lanka)
title: The most heavenly place in Sri Lanka

body: We had a party of 11 visiting HP. We were lucky with weather as from Nuwara Eiyla up to gate of the park we were in fog, but when we reached the start of the trek the clouds cleared and we enjoyed all the views during the walk. The walk takes 3 hours and takes you on a path with great views that you cannot see in Europe. If you travel as a number of families please buy group tictet. We got approx 25% discount for 11 tickets (4 kids and 7 adults). Overall good experience worth waiking up at 5am
title: Goos time out

body: We enjoyed our walk at Horton Plains. We left Nuwara Eliya at 5am to catch the sunrise as we were driving up to the park, however it was unfortunately obscured by cloud. The walk was great at that time of day though, not too hot, and Bakers Falls are quite stunning! Also saw Samba deer, squirrels and birds. An easy 3 hour walk.
title: Nice walk to get some exercise and beautiful waterfall

body: Nice walk, but nothing special. World’s end is very beautiful, so this makes it up patly. We started at 12h and had no rain or fog. We were recommended to start at 5 am but kindly rejected. Maybe we were lucky but we didn’t see any rain. The hike was 3h30 and quite difficult, but doable if you have an average condition.We took the opposite direction, so first to the falls.
title: Nice walk with beautiful view

body: Very nice and best place to hiking and can see many bird nice valley good air nice breathing we enjoyed well how we need
title: Best hiking which i did

body: This national park is the source for four of Sri Lanka's major rivers, so it's not unusual to experience a bit of rain. Fortunately, the heavy rain dropped the night before our 9.5 km trek through the park, which took in the spectacular World's End. It made some uneven parts of the trail a bit slippery, so solid hiking shoes or, at minimum runners, are essential.Only a moderate level of fitness is required to navigate the main trail, which takes in World's End and Bakers Falls. However, anyone with some walking or climbing disability should take note that there are those uneven areas to negotiate. World's End is so called because of its 900 metre vertical cliff face that drops into the forest of the valley wall. It's hard to capture its scale in photographs. There are two viewing decks at World's End. Beware, particularly for children, that there are few barriers to prevent falls over the cliffs, both on the decks and on the short trail between decks. My impression was that the coiled razor wire would merely lacerate you during the fall rather than prevent it. The higher deck gives a much better view of the main cliff face. The steps down to Bakers Falls are also quite steep.Hortons Plains features a wide variety of landscape and an explosion of different colours from the many plant species that adorn the plain. The area is also a good place to see Sambar Deer, one of Sri Lanka's larger deer species.
title: A trek worth making

body: I was traveling alone and staying in a guest house in Nuwara Eliya so my transportation was arranged for by my wonderful hosts, but my tour guide/driver picked me up at 5am to take me out to Horton Plains. We got there early a) to beat the crowds, and b) because I had an afternoon train to Ella to catch, but we actually got there so early that the ticket office hadn't opened yet. The hike isn't too difficult, it's about 8 miles with a few portions of steeper climbing, but getting there in the morning allows you to see some GORGEOUS views. My driver gave me the tip of sitting and waiting at World's End because a lot can change in the scenery in a matter of minutes, and it was the best advice. I ate snacks I packed (remember to do this) and took a 40 minute rest up there and watched in awe as clouds and fog came in and out (at one point completely blocking the view and then clearing up to reveal a gorgeous drop and the plains beyond). I wanted to take pictures every time I turned the corner because I was treated to new views every mile or so - the diversity in ecosystems and flora/fauna is INSANE. If you're in Nuwara Eliya, make sure you make time for this hike! I actually stopped in Nuwara Eliya JUST so I could get out here! Definitely get an early start (apparently sometimes in the morning you can see deer and elephants if it's early enough!) so you're hiking when it's cooler and to beat the crowds.
title: Great morning hike

body: The view in this park is so breathtaking and mesmerising!!!! The ticket price to pay is worth it- this is a must visit!!!! We felt small in this park, we felt refreshed! This was definitely life changing!!!!
title: The best memorable experience ever!

body: During our stay at Nuwara Elyia we went to the Horton Plains to hike the worlds end trail. Beautiful trail which is around a 3 hour walk... not very steep and good temperatures around there.As we are resident the entrance fee was low, but for foreigners, for which the entrance fee is higher, we still recommend this park. It is completely different than the rest of Sri Lanka with other surroundings and lower temperatures (around 22 C during day time)
title: Worlds end nice walk

body: Recommended for those who love trekking as it has a 9 km walk to reach the Baker's Falls and the cliff.
title: Nature trail

body: We had a very unfortunate experience when buying tickets to enter Horton Plains National Park. We visited on the morning of Friday 12th July. Apologies for the long and less than positive review, I am also posting this hoping someone may be able to point me towards a way to lodge a complaint with the Park itself as I haven’t been able to find this online. Ticket prices are not advertised as prices tend to fluctuate so there is no price list at the ticket booth. We asked for “3 tickets, one person is local”, however this was interpreted as 3 tickets plus one local. A foreigner ticket at the time was ~2,650 rupees. With no price list, visitors the transaction is based purely on verbal communication with no calculator or screen to show how prices are calculated (there are three taxes on top of the ticket price). Understandably this is also a quick, rushed process during busy times such as when we visited.Unfortunately, we were unable to realise we were overcharged until we had driven 10 minutes from the ticket office to the park entrance. At the park entrance we spoke with a number of staff and based on what they advised we decided to enter the park rather than drive back and seek a refund (lucky we did this because as we found out, we would not have been refunded anyway and it would have ruined our visit). On our way out we approached the ticket booth and fortunately the same cashier was working (a middle aged man, moustache, larger, has worked at the park for over 15 years). We were very careful to politely inform that we were accidentally overcharged (e.g. we avoided saying “you overcharged us”, instead saying “we were accidentally overcharged”) however he immediately went on the defensive, became very rude and irrational and refused to help us. He accused us of being irresponsible and not communicating with him properly. He also said there is no possibility of a refund once a sale has been made and its the customers responsibility to know what they are being charged and that he does not make mistakes so it must be our fault. When we tried to explain that we were not trying to pass blame and a simple misunderstanding had occurred, he became argumentative and started insulting our tour guide/driver in Sinhalese and saying he was not looking after us properly. He refused to call the park manager (he said there was no phone reception, although all three of us had reception) and said nobody would help us because it was our fault. There was lots of back and forth about ticket prices not being advertised, no way of knowing what we have been charged for until transaction has been finalised etc. until we finally decided that nothing we did or said would help us obtain a refund. Overall, this left a very sour taste in our mouths and our tour guide/driver felt ashamed that a park ranger would behave in this way. Unfortunately, the cashier did not have an ounce of empathy and his behaviour screamed dishonesty and not a care on the world for doing what is right. Had he at least even tried to help us in the slightest, our experience with him would have been completely difference. Lesson: when buying tickets and you have a local guide to accompany you, be very clear to say X foreigner tickets and Y local ticket. Avoid assuming any statements like “3 people, one is local” as this will be interpreted as 3 foreigners, one local”.As for the park itself, it is beautiful and the views are amazing. It was lovely walking through such stunning scenery. However, the price is quite high especially in comparison to similar yet free experiences we have had in Sri Lanka as well as other national parks we have visited around the world.
title: Terrible experience buying tickets

body: Good for childrens also. Helpful staff. Big parking space for bikes,car, van and mini bus 🚌. Bring your passport or identification card

body: Do not miss doing this trek and experiencing the true unspoiled beauty of Sri Lanka. It is an amazing experience about 2hrs walk one way.

body: Left hotel at dawn to get there before it’s too hot. The road is good until the train station and then become bumpy. We had a 4*4 all the way from the hotel. The park is beautiful. It’s a moderate intensity trek. Take some food and water. No snacks and juice box are allowed so fruit and water are recommended. The meadow is beautiful and “worlds end” is a very nice view point. Don’t miss this park.
title: Beautiful nature reserve

body: Had a really great time walking around this NP. Started early morning but already a lot of people. (You can let your luggage or some bags a the entry checkpoint if needed)Awesome views. Some of the greatest views are a bit further than where everybody is. (Signs are there) Walk is a bit more tricky but worth it!
