body: Horton Plains is a gently undulating highland plateau at 2,100.meters above sea level of Sri Lanka,lying at the south end of the central highlands. It is dominated by Kirigalpoththa (2.389 meters) to west and Totupolakanda (2,357 meters) to the north. Kirigalpoththa and Totupolakanda are the second and third highest mountains in Sri Lanaka. Tha charm of the plateau and encircling mountain range, often concealed mist, is enhanced by Baker's Falls and the two two escarpments, Small Worlds End (274 meters) and Big Worlds End (884 meters). The plateau is drained by tributaries of Mahaweli Ganga (main river of Sri Lanka) to the north (Agra Oya) and the Walawe Ganga to the south (Belihul Oya), serving as an important catchment area for these two rivers which have been harnessed for irrigation and hydro power. This plateau consists of many Amphibians, three types of harmless reptiles, birds and mammals including the leopard. Access to the plains are mainly from Ohiya, Pattipola and Nuwara Eliya. There are foot trails from Nagarak Trail is from the Agrapathana - Diyagama Tea Estate and also from Belihul Oya which falls into the same Nagarak Trail. This is place you must visit and possible to camp in the camping site. Plenty of Wildlife and ideal location for a wildlife photographer like me who is looking for adventure .
title: "HEAVEN ON EARTH"

body: Its a long journey to reach there but the scenic is so beautiful all the way. You should start early morning to avoid sun heat. its 9km trail but just amazing as the its muddy, rocky & watrery. Water fall is just out of the world. the experience is just amazing and feels very good once you are done with.
title: Best Trail I have done

body: Cool breezes and lovely views! Make sure you bring a light jacket for the early AM. Wear comfortable shoes! Great photography opportunities!
title: Excellent day of hiking!

body: This is perfect location to see rare birds endemic to Sri Lanka while walking among montane forests.
title: Explore cloud forests in Sri Lanka

body: We love this place. Love the plains, cost USD22 to enter and be careful of the ticketing guy as he attempted to scam us. Check the receipts and the change.Your bags will be checked for plastics, no drones allowed.
title: Lovely

body: Another great creation of Mother Nature !! Nice place to explore.Worlds End, Bakers Fall, Endangered Species
title: Natural Beauty

body: Good trekking and scenery . Must wake up and go there as early in the morning in the dark as we leave hotel at 5am but when we get there, there was a big crowd there already. It will get hotter and we complete the trek at 1pm which is very hot .
title: Start early on Horton Plains National Park to stay cool

body: You witness a vast range of bio-diversity here , most of the plants here are endemic ones. Great views are there if you are lucky to reach worlds end before the mist covers everything,do not forget to take the rain covers
title: Cloud forest

body: Takes some traveling to get to, but nice place to hike only because it is so different than other places around Sri Lanka. The views are nice, the waterfall is ok. Really, it is a nice 9 km hike through fields and thick forest. Don’t bring anything plastic, except water bottles because they take the plastic from you-be prepared to have your bag searched.
title: Nice hike

body: We visited Horton Plains during our Srilanka trip this week. Visiting Horton plains is both expensive and time consuming affair. You should read and understand what to expect there and then plan your visit if you still see a value.What to expect at horton plains?8 kms of walking trail, with 2 viewpoints, 1 waterfalls, few pools and lots of greenery all aroundA steep fee of USD 20 per personAlmost a full day of time (4 hours to explore the trail, 1-2 hours to reach Horton Plains from Nuwara Eliyabasic facilities for toilet, food available. Walking path has boulders and narrow sections-not very suitable for elders or small kids.Horton Plains is a very scenic place- no doubt on that. Greenery in every direction, cool breeze makes the walk memorable. You can refill your bottles from freshwater streams. If you have a day to spare, love nature and have a transportation then do visit. Check my blog for detailed photos and reviews.
title: Scenic place with 20 USD fee

body: it is wonderful place to visit .we enjoyed lot, if you visit the nuwara eliya must visit this place. it from nuwara eliya above 45 mints. from there needs be work out around nine km. anyway we enjoyed lot.
title: Amazing place

body: Was a very easy trek with so much beautiful scenery, you don’t need a guide and just follow the trails. We saw leopard foot prints from across one of the trails we were trekking which was very exciting! I’d come back again!
title: A must go!

body: The walk to worlds end and Bakers Falls was around 9km. It was a great hike along a pathway. We arrived at mini worlds end around 0830 and unfortunately the heavy mist didn't allow us to see anything. We headed to worlds end as the must cleared which allowed glorious views of the valley but within 25 minutes the must came in again.It was a really enjoyable walk/hike despite the drizzle and would highly recommended a visit
title: Great views if you are lucky

body: We traveled from central nuwara eliya early in the morning and start trekking around 6am.The plain is magical with mist and fog hanging high and low. Depending on luck you will spot a deer or two. You will hear all sorts of sound from the woods, birds, bugs, distant streams.The walk in general is quite easy, no major climb, mainly flat. Some areas are a little rocky, quite wet and slippery after rain/fog. On a steady pace the loop is about 3hours.Will highly recommend it to everyone. We had a very good time.
title: Magical gem within the hill country

body: The views are amazing and well worth the 5 stars but the tracks around the area are more likely a 2 and in places very challenging and it appears that in June/July there are a lot of wash-aways which means you need to climb over boulders or walk in amongst what looks like stream beds. Do make sure that you get there early in the morning. We had to wait at little worlds end for the mist to lift but the wait was well worth it for the view and then another challenging walk to Worlds End for even more amazing views. Toilets were really poor with broken doors, broken cisterns that made them almost unusable. A lot of the steps in the area were also badly washed away which is where the challenge comes into it.
title: Horton Plains/ Worlds Ens

body: I arranged a tuk-tuk with my homestay in Haputale to go here very early one mid-week morning. This cost 2500lkr, as the drive is over an hour and the tuk-tuk driver waited for 3hrs (return trip). Entrance to the park is expensive, probably too expensive, but there is no way of avoiding this. However, the circular 9km hike once you're within the park is very rewarding. The path is fairly challenging as there are a range of terrains, from sandy red coloured rocky river-bed style paths, narrow paths with 4000ft drops at one side, and flat ordinary trails along the plains. There is much wildlife to see, as well as the views. As for the plains, they looked not unlike the Yorkshire Dales in England, except with Rhododendron bushes! This area was a refreshing change of terrain from the endless yet beautiful hill views which are common in the area. Make sure you get there between 06:00 - 07:00 am to get the most out of the views. Cloud cover usually lifts at this time, then falls again a few hour later. Despite this, the views are only part of the experience. For me, the hike was the most enjoyable aspect of the visit, as well as the unusual early morning jungle sounds.
title: A wonderful experience of varying landscapes. A must see!

body: Best trekking place in Srilanka with a diverse geography. We enjoyed this part of the trip very much
title: Very good place

body: Best mountain walk exercise. only problem was the entrance ticket and service charge is much high. no clean toilets for the service charge you pay for tickets.
title: Best Trekking path with hot misty mountains.

body: We were lucky to be there when the morning fog cleared. The place was just scenic. The experience of criss-crossing through the grasslands, forests, falls and finally out to the open again was invigorating.
title: Eliya's unmistakable spot!

body: Everyone told us the best chance of seeing Worlds End (a view from the top of a cliff edge looking down into the valley of a small town which is picturesque) was to go very early in the morning. We were so tired from climbing Adam peak the following day and having no sleep we opted for a longer lay in so only got to Norton Plains as 7.45am. Saying that the weather that day wasn’t the best but it least it was dry. The 9km walk though was lovely. We basically had the whole park to ourselves (we saw maybe 20 people during our visit) and it was picturesque, beautifully quiet and the local wildlife were so used to people that they would come over to you or at least not run away when you approached.So did we get to see Worlds End? Unfortunately not, but whether we got up really early and chanced it or did what we did I think the chances for that day was limited due to the time of year. What I will say though is it didn’t take away the enjoyment we had of walking around the route, seeing the wildlife and experiencing the quietness. You will need to hire a driver and a jeep to get there as the roads aren’t great but most hotels will do that for you.
title: Beautiful, chilled and cloudy

body: This is a national park and protected zone full of vegetation, water falls, lot of animals and birds, wonderful place for nature lovers and camping, I spent the whole day exploring the reserve, not to be missed if you on a holiday visiting Nuwara eliya.
title: A heaven for nature lovers

body: The place is accessible only by private car and the road is steep and narrow, moreover its around 1.5 hour journey from Nuwara Eliya. Then the entrance ticket price is too high according to me, which along with car cost makees an expensive trp.But its worth it! The mountains, waterfalls, jungles and deers...all make it up for the money.Wear comfortable hiking shoes, and better to avoid if physically unfit.i would like more signs in the planes, we got lost a couple of times.
title: Wonderful World's end and much more, but only for nature lovers!

body: It’s a very early start because you need to complete the walk before it gets too hot. But, it’s very cold at 05:00 so wear layers: I wore two t-shirts, a hoody and a waterproof and de-layered as the sun started to rise. You need good walking shoes really. We saw a guy go over on his ankle (it’s quite rocky in places) and really struggle. Be very careful when you get to the World’s End viewing points. Lots of people perch on the edge doing yoga poses but it’s very dangerous. The wind can whip up from nowhere and someone has died there. Make sure you take a packed breakfast but don’t take any plastic. They check your bags as you go in and remove the labels from water bottles and the straws from juice cartons, which is to be applauded.
title: Really enjoyed this 9k walk to World’s End

body: Its a nice place for walking. Along the way there are waterfalls. May not be ideal if you are with chidren. The walk to the world's end takes about 2-3 hours depending your speed. You also may see deers and other animals. Nice peaceful walk thru nature.
title: Nice, serene place

body: Climbing through very narrow roads, the vehicle strained a lot, but the top views were hilarious. Too expensive, unless you plan serious trekking alongside. The drives are really charming
title: Fantastic trip

body: A visit to the Horton Plains should be a must for Tourists to enjoy the fresh air and nature at its best. Walking, hiking, looking at the flora and fauna is pure pleasure. Only those who are fit as there could be some distance walking and climbing to do. It is worth the effort. Guided walking tours are available
title: Tranquillity at its best

body: If you love nature and some kind of walking, hiking this is ideal. Not suitable for elders who can't walk few Kms. So for hiking lovers this is a good one. It's just some walking. Not hiking. But need some strength. You have to buy tickets to enter. This is like a management fee. A small amount. Nature is so lovely and nice. It's so silent, Do not break the silence in here. If you are afraid of sunburn use sun cream, sunglasses and get some drinking water for your visit. along with a hat may be.
title: Breathtaking View

body: This a definite must visit if you are in the area. Very pretty scenery. In addition to the Plain itself, you can access Mini Worlds End, Worlds End and Bakers Falls via a hike. Keep at least 04-05 hours for the whole walk around the Plain if you hope to complete the full trail.Note - no plastic items are allowed inside the Plain.
title: Worth a visit for sure!

body: Initially we were decidedly sceptical about putting going to Horton's Plains. There was not one, but many reasons for that. To go to Horton’s Plains one has to start early. In fact, as early as 5AM and for that we would have to wake up at least at 4AM. Not to mention the unbearable cold outside. On top of that, Horton plains had a lot of mixed reviews about the walks and the views it offered. All that too for a extravagant entrance fees. We were struggling with the thought of waking up that early and going out in the cold on a long walk where the possibility of views being completely blocked by the clouds was high. But then on the other hand, we did wish to go ahead with the plan, given that we had come all the way along.At the end, we did go there. After a drive of an hour and a half, we reached the entrance where we booked the tickets, and paid the cab entrance fees. Even at that time, the place was overly crowded with tourists and their vehicles. A heavy fog was around. We thought we were prepared for the cold. As suggested by a few blogs, I was wearing 5 layers of warm clothing. We got off the cab and went to join the long queue for the entrance tickets. The cold was unbearable and soon we were shivering. Thankfully the tickets were finally sorted out and we got back in the cab, to drive towards the entrance gate. The fog had slowly started to clear up as we started with the walk. It was a three hour closed trail, a simple trek with a little up and down slopes and a little rocky patches here and there. Nothing scary. The fog is basically created by cloud forests in the Horton’s plains. Luckily enough, the sun popped out of the clouds, clearing up the fog. The Baker’s falls offered a pretty view. We got clear, unhindered views form World’s end view point. What Luck! But then, the views were actually not that impressive. And the walk was not that challenging. I would like to mention one impressive thing about the management of Horton plains. At the entrance, they have a baggage check point where no tourist is allowed to proceed with a piece of plastic, may it be a bag or a bottle or a chewing gum box, thus keeping Horton plains plastic free. I think this is a very sensible step and ideally should be followed everywhere around the world.
title: Over-hyped may be?

body: Go there early, as early as you can, to beat the mist. Wear comfortable footwear and your bottles of water cannot be covered with paper.It's a lot of walking, climbing and will require you to be moderately fit. We did the whole shebang including the falls, and that took us about 3 hours. Once you arrive, you have two options, either to continue straight or go left, we went left. Our guide said we should reach the little and big world's ends before 9:30 so the mist doesn't settle in and he was right. If we had been 15 minutes late, we wouldn't have seen anything. The mist covered the whole area 5 minutes after we were done taking pictures. It was beautiful to see the cloudy body follow us and then cover us as we continued trekking throughout the planes. You can take a snack with you and eat it on top of big world's end, it's a beautiful place, cannot describe it in words. Really worth the visit and the workout !
title: Breathtaking views - exhausting climb

body: The walk through the Horton Plains National Park was gorgeous. Nature pure, amazing fews from World’s End and Little World’s End! Highly recommended!
title: Very nice walk through nature

body: The 9km route is relatively easy, with mostly flat terrain but a few patches of bouldering and climbing that does make it trickier in parts. Allow for about 3 to 3.5 hours if you stick to the path (we veered off a bit and extended our walk off the beaten track). The viewpoints are quite spectacular and the surroundings serene. A worthwhile excursion.
title: A beautiful and thoroughly enjoyable hike.

body: A great opportunity to enjoy the splendor of nature and spend the day actively!Wake up early, obligatory comfortable shoes,headcover, protective cream, sunglasses and drinking water. If you arrive early, you need a jacket, in the morning in early May it was cool.Before entering the territory of the reserve, a ticket office with a queue for 10 - 20 minutes. We were with a personal guide who took care of entrance tickets but you can go by yourself (get lost if you do not turn off the way is impossible). There is a parking before the start of the route, where both the touristic and personal cars park. There is also a cafe that looks rather suspicious, but our guide said that it is possible to have a tea and eat traditional pastries. It was not bad!The toilet is located at the back of the cafe, it is better to visit it, because there are no more lavatories on the entire route.Despite the clouds during the entire walk and a fairly cool temperature in the morning in the first 2 hours, the noses and cheeks burned, so you must always apply a protective cream, then a walk of at least 9 km will be comfortable and enjoyable.The road in places is sometimes rather stony and difficult, therefore it is better to choose another occupation for children and people with limited motor abilities.The nature is amazing, the silence, the singing of birds and the murmur of water in streams, passing into small rivers and waterfalls are interrupted only by groups of passing tourists. Early in the morning saw one deer and several roe deer grazing not so far from the cafe. On the way there were chameleons and earthen small lizards, many birds. We did not hurry, we admired the surrounding nature for a long time, and after 6 hours we completed the ring of the route.A nice rest for everyone who is going to Horton Plains!
title: 9 kilometers walk

body: This was one of my highlights in Sri Lanka! The views are incredible! The walk is very enjoyable! Make sure to get there early so you can enjoy all the view before the mist rolls in! I would consider this a must if visiting Sri Lanka!
title: Amazing

body: It was a lovely hike to view worlds end and mini worlds end. Loved the view.Would recommend bringing water, and wearing proper shoes. Also snacks! It s advised to go during early morning and not late evenings.The view is worth the climb.
title: Amazing Hike

body: Loved the loop hike. Go early to avoid crowd we were at the gate at 6. Really nice hike seeng World Ends, waterfall and nature at its best. Absolutely no plastic is allowed past the starting point and I am very impressed. They checked our backpacks and removed even plastic labels from water bottle! The hike was plastic free so I think it's a great idea!!
title: Fantastic hike

body: We left at 5:30 am from our hotel in nuwara Eliya to start our hike at 7am. The journey was around an hour in a TUK TUK (2500rps return journey) with 30 mins cueing. Most people come at this time to avoid peak heat and to see the views at worlds end without clouds. The route although not sign posted well can be done easily without a guide. Don’t worry there’ll be plenty of walkers around from all ages doing the walk at the ungodly hour. You can choose 2 routes:route 1 is the one to your left and goes straight when you reach it. This will take you to mini worlds end, worlds end and bakers fall in that order. Plus point - you’ll def get to the main attraction without clouds. Down side is you’ll have a harder trek back uphill. Route 2- this is the one we chose. The path when you reach the first bifurcation is the one going down the steps ahead of you. This will lead you to bakers falls, worlds end and mini worlds end in this order. Plus point - it’s an easier journey back as it’s mainly downhill returning. Down side - by the time we got to mini worlds end it was so cloudy we couldn’t see the view! Either way both routes are around 11 km loop. It’s relatively easy- just feels very long and you get hot! Took us 4 hours at a leisurely pace. Make sure you get your hotel to pack you a breakfast box so you can eat it when you’re having a break there. The cost of the ticket depends on how many of you are there in your group- the more of you going the cheaper it will be individually. For 2 of us it cost 3315 each ( including our TUK TUK drivers entrance). If you’re in Nuwara Eliya a visit isn’t complete without a hike in hortons plain. The view from worlds end is AMAZING!
title: Worth the walk !

body: its an amazing place to be. i was told that you need to be at the plains by 6 o'clock as soon as the park opens to have a quiet view of the trail and mother nature. leaving by 4.30 totally worth it. i reached in time and its not like no-one was there, but very few. totally enjoyes the sun rise and then the trail on the park is beautiful as well. do remember that it gets crowded by 10'ish and youight want to avoid that. its almost 8 kilometers trail and it takes around 3 hours very easily even when you are continuously walking. stay healthy ppl!!!
title: money worth spent and getting uo early totally worth it

body: Horton Plains is worth visiting if you do enjoy a good hike. Also; the landscapes are beautiful and very different from what you'll see in other parts of Sri Lanka. It is a bit pricey though, and I wouldn't recommend visiting Horton Plains for World's End alone. If you're not that much into nature or walking: don't come here! You can see equally impressive or better views for free at other places in Sri Lanka and it'll save you the money and time to get there. People with mobility problems may find this hike less enjoyable, because the trail can be challenging in places and paths can get slippery after rainfall.
title: Very nice walk, but you can get equally impressive views for free in other places

body: We arrived at 6am in order to walk to World's End before mist came down. We had a fantastic 10km walk and the views from World's End were truly stupendous. We saw a few birds but not much more by way of wildlife. Nonetheless, the walk was a highlight of our trip to Sri Lanka.There is a small exhibition and (paid) toilets. I was a bit miffed to see that the exhibition asks what damage you have done by visiting the park that day: if visitor numbers are such a concern, then perhaps pricing and entrance policies should be amended rather than passively criticising the people who have paid $25 for the privilege of visiting the park.
title: Fantastic views

body: If you're into walking I would highly recommend the walk through Horton Plains to World's End! The scenery is beautiful! There are rolling hills, a beautiful waterfall and spectacular views from both World's End and Mini World's End.Tips:- Go early! The walk takes about 3 hours in total and about 1.5 hours from the starting Point to reach World's End (the main viewing point) We left our hotel in Newara Eliya at 5.30 and started walking at 7am.- Wear runners and comfortable clothes - I'd recommend layers (as it can be chilly at 7am and very warm by 9am). We were lucky with the weather but apparently it rains at lot so bring a raincoat).- Do the walk anti-clockwise! There's a main path from the carpark up to the start of the loop. At the sign board go straight ahead (most people to left). The first part of the walk is open to the elements so offers beautiful views as the sun rises and it's nicer to do this part of the walk when it's a little cooler (If you walk in the other direction there is little shelter from the sun as you're returning). Also there are less crowds at the waterfall!
title: Beautiful scenery

body: The trek is around 10 km ... the place is around an hours drive from nuwara Eliya . Try and head out early cos if u r late the views at the worlds end would be covered in mist . We did the trek at the end of march the weather was pretty good . Carry a bottle of water and some light snacks as there is nothing available on the route inside . A small shop located outside sells water biscuits and basic Sri Lankan snacks
title: Nice trek

body: I was there with my family during the sinhala/tamil new year season. Perhaps due to season in Nuwara Eliya the park was absolutely crowded. Which we did not like that much but i think this is not something we can't avoid. However the park was spectacular as ever. weather was very kind to us in everyway. We had a perfect day.
title: Bit crowded but amazing

body: We reached around 11.30AM there as we were travelling from Kandy!! I went with two of my Sri Lankan friends and I felt foreign ticket is overpriced as no where close to them.It's around 9kms walk inside the forest which seems easy as nature at its best. First we saw Mini world end and 500mts above world end and scenery is stunning. Best time to go is before afternoon as mist will be covered after that.Best thing is Bakers waterfalls which is beautiful and don't feel like moving out from there. Stunning view all-around the walk. It was raining heavily half through our walk but we continued walking in the rain.Spend enough time inside as nature beauty is amazing. Take enough water during the walk. Wear shoes as most of the rocks are slippery. Take umbrella in case of rain as there is no shades inside the forest.
title: Worth a long walk inside the forests

body: We went to the park from the Heritance Tea Factory Hotel where we set off at 0445 to get there before the park opened at 0600. Dawn was breaking on a misty morning. We were soon joined by other vehicles but an early star is recommended to avoid the heat. Paths are a bit rough and were pleased we wore proper hiking shoes. It is very hilly but the views are well worth it, Expect to take 5 - 6 hours of hard walking. Our guide took us to Baker Falls which was a good place to cool off with the spray from the falls.
title: An early start is recommended to see the sun come out and enjoy the views

body: We got up at 4.30 to arrive extra early to spend several hours walking through the national park and to see mini world's end and world's end. Incredible scenery, wildlife and dramatic cliff like drops. Such a nice relief from the hustle and bustle of the rest of the island and such wonderful respite from the shocking litter everywhere else. At least here we could appreciate the outstanding beauty of the island without extraordinary levels of litter and marketing hoardings. Wear suitable walking boots/shoes.
title: Beauty, wildlife, worlds end and much much more

body: As I live in Sri lanka for couple of months already I do know the prices around. Horton Plains was on my list since I'm a nature lover. However even though I went there with a local, at the entrance they have tried to overcharge even him for the simple fact of being with me,a "foreigner",they have asked somewhere close to 6000 rupees only for one person! We got really pissed as the entrance fee kept changing from 4200 to 7000 in just 5 minutes. In the end we left really annoyed and found other peak to climb. There are many other places around that area that are still so beautiful and for free so don't let yourself being fooled just for a few hrs walk!P.S. We managed to see different birds and even plenty of monkeys everywhere else we went around there, is not just Horton Plains that has it so spare your money if you can.
title: Way too pricey! Beware

body: I would give this a 5 stars but there are a couple of reasons that made this not quite the ultimate experience.Let me give you the reasons why you SHOULD go:This simply a nice and breathtaking park. The scenery is lovely, the trail is nice, the hike is very easy and the park is very strict on littering policies.What you should know before you plan on going:Plan in advance and get there EARLY. The drive from Nuwara Elyia was at least an hour. We were told that if we wanted to see World's End (the nicest view of the valley) we needed to do the first half of the hike before 10 am because after that it's so cloudy you won't see anything. Also the big tours start at 7:30 am and the trails are crowded with people. So you basically need to be there when the park opens at 6am. So if you have an hour drive to do.... you need to leave at 5am.... you get the picture.The line at the entrance of the park was insane. We had to wait at least 30 minutes to get out tickets.The first part of the trail was nice, but after an hour or so, it started to get crowded...A LOT. I will sound mean but, WHY in hell do people think it's OK to go in NATURE to see animals and scenery and YELL and blast their MUSIC on their phone for everyone to hear? The park itself was beautiful, but the tourists ruined the whole experience for me. This place has become a big touristy attraction and the amount of people being disrespectful was insane.It's my opinion but the park should limit the amount of tourists they let in at a time.
title: Beautiful hike, although...

body: the drive from nuwara eliya to the plains early morning is very scenic. the plains are made interesting by signs along route. the worlds end view is average.
title: interesting 10km trail

body: Horton Plains is a great place to discover Sri Lanka's outdoors. Rare cloud forest, open plains, waterfalls and a terrific view off of World's End viewpoint (only in the early morning) all in the easy highland climate. We were lucky having been guided by Nimal, the most knowledgeable guide we met in our 3 week stay in Sri Lanka. He has abundant knowledge of flora and fauna (explained to us plenty of plants and showed us animals), but also of all the other things we wanted to learn about (any place or thing in) Sri Lanka. Thanks to his great English, we have learned a lot during this half day trip of the Horton Plains. He is smart, helpful and kind, you felt like he's always got your back and he knows exactly what tourists like!Thank you Nimal for making this trip such a good experience!
title: Horton Plains hike with guide Nimal

body: Horton Plains National Park is a good place to visit even though the entrance fee is quite high and service is poor. We arrived at the gate at 6 am (just open) and there were already many people. The 9 km walk is not difficult and there is a lot to see and to hear when other visitors keep quiet which is not always the case. Park authorities should use some of the money they receive to improve ways and toilets!
title: Like another world

body: We love our morning at hortain plains Go early .Did the Horton plains trekking. Beautiful views so worth a visit. Well preserved by staff ... check your bag for plastic packaging as dropping of litter strongly discouraged. .. It's easy to follow the path. Best time to visit early morning late afternoon as it's a good 5 miles on the circular route very nice beautiful place location was superb
title: Horton plains

body: Are you sick of all the rubbish too? We often thought, man, why dont they do something about that and protect at least some landscapes? Here, however, they do. And that was the first impression we got from the park itself.The private booked drive up here from nuwara eliya was about an hour long and pretty curvy, but alright. On the entrance the staff checked all our bags for rubbish and asked to throw it away. The walk was awesome, not only because of the weather, but also because of the great welcoming by a majestic dear right on our way! The countryside invites to take Photos and rest in a quiet surrounding. The worlds end was pretty impressive, even the 'little' one. The big one... well, you got to see it yourself! But take care, its a long way down there.The whole walk ended with a beautiful waterfall... wow, what a day! I tell you, it is totally worth it. We've been for five weeks in sri lanka, and this was one of our favorite trips. The quitness and peace up there is something you dont find in sri lanka at every corner.However, here a tip:Pack your food in boxes or paper and Your drinks in bottles (not those tetra packs). Otherwise you'll get to throw it away at the entrance.
title: Nice Walk to the end of the world!

body: One of my key highlights of Sri Lanka trip ! Totally enjoyed the hike - was initially worried that it might be too strenuous but it was manageable. Recommend to go early to catch sunrise and the fantastic view. Be prepared for the change in weather too - Low temp in the early morning and hot humid temp in mid/ late morning.
title: Strongly recommended

body: Our group went to the Horton Plains for a recommended hike leaving our hotel early in the morning when it was very misty. However this is a good time to start the trek but beware it can be quite cold so be prepared for some cold and wet weather. It is lovely trek of approximately 9k and is not very difficult if you are quite fit and used to walking. The scenery is amazing especially at the summit (The Worlds End) and the overall views beautiful. Did not see much wildlife but not sure I expected to as there is a significant number of people on the trek. It is well worth doing just for the trek and the scenery.
title: Awesome hike

body: It’s an easy plain hike with good views en route. Arrive early morning - before 7am. Try to take the left path - sun will be on your back, you will beat crowd, and go opposite the set flow. Pack snacks. Do not litter.
title: Easy, rewarding hike with Sambar spotting

body: Great place to hike through wonderful scenery. The views at the summit are spectacular and well worth the effort. Please abide by the signs not to feed the wildlife.
title: End of the world

body: I went with a driver who helped buy my ticket and showed me the way and then I hiked around the trial by myself. The hike is about 9 km and since I stopped to take photos it toom almost 3 hours. The path is easy to follow and as long as you have an average fitness level you should havr no problems. There are a few areas where you will be walking down/up a path that has rocks in the way or tree roots (the tree root area was the steepest). The path to Baker's falls is stairs.The scenery is worth the hike and going early in the morning is a good idea as its usually the clearest time. Side note: its a but chilly (12 C) in the early morning and most people wore a jacket for at least the beginning part of the hike
title: Beautiful hike

body: Unbelievable place.... Today the weather was amazing and it started to rain after 2 pm, heavily rain... you need a hiking boots specially if there is a chance for raining ... but you don't need a guide, all the road marked and you can easily recognise the walking routes, take enough drinking water with you for about 4 hours, tissue, and something to keep mosquitos away from you, there is a special wet wipes for that, if you like to explore it more just incase buy a map for the park from the entrance office or print it out from Google maps, it's even much better, I used it Today. Great experience, if you did not explore Horton plains while you are in Sri Lanka, you really waste your time and money!
title: Peice of heaven!

body: The Nationalpark is very clean, people working there take care that you do not litter. Which I think is a great spirit. The walkaround to go to the different sites can be done in 2-3 hours, depending on how fast you walk and how long you linger at the different spots. If you go in the mornings, which you should do since otherwise the fog will come in from the coast, there is a big queue at the entrance. You have to queue approx. 20 - 30 minutes. And then there are of course a lot of tourists on the walk around, but that´s to be expected. Nevertheless it is beautiful and worth it.
title: Great and clean Nationalpark

body: This was without doubt one of our favourite trips in Sri Lanka. We left Nuwara Eliya at 5:00 to get there early enough to beat the crowds and heat. Our driver came with us as he understandably preferred walking around a beautiful national park over sitting in his car. This was good as he provided some snippets of information and history and told us his preferred route around (left/clockwise) We particularly enjoyed little world's end as it was quieter and had equally amazing views. If visiting Sri Lanka this should be a must do as the scenery is incredibly beautiful.
title: A must do in Sri Lanka

body: One thing I loved about this walk is that there are no guard rails- walkers were responsible for their own welfare. Plastic was confiscated at the entrance. We had some small fruit in a plastic bag which they transferred into a paper bag. I had trouble breathing while doing the climbs, but thoroughly enjoyed the walk as a whole.
title: Lovely walk

body: I loved the hike and the misty hills. Learnt quite a bit about cloud forests and my friends even spotted a leopard on our way back.
title: Enjoyed the hike

body: We cought the perfect day; clear and sunny. The scenery is very beautiful. We visited this area with a tuk-tuk which I really like as you are basically sitting outside enjoying the views.
title: Beautiful

body: The circular trail is 8km long and on average takes 3 hours to complete which allows time for a breakfast picnic / photographs / simply admiring the views. There is no need for a guide and I'm not even sure they are available such is the trail so easy to follow. An early start is required as apparently the cloud comes in daily mid morning onwards. Temperature was fine even at the 6.30 start (light jacket) and once you get going and the sun warms up, you are soon peeling back the layers to just t-shirt. Very enjoyable and not too taxing - we're in our 50s!
title: A really enjoyable hike taking in beautiful scenery

body: This place needs your early morning attendance. If you are a mountain person and love to trekking - this is the place for you. Just gear up with sports shoes and joggers. It has mini world ends and all beauty surrounded with mountains and fog.
title: Beautiful mornings

body: Did the whole hike early in the morning. Great scenery during the hike and would recommend if in the area
title: Interesting hike

body: Everyone crowds here at about 6am - seemingly after about 10 the clouds come in and you can't see much.The views are stunning from worlds end, and a great place to sit and eat a picnic breakfast.The walk itself is fairly obvious, some slightly tricky bits up and down rough terrain so wear sturdy footwear and take water etc. It's about 10k for the whole round trip, and it took us about 2.5 hours including a 20 minute sit down at worlds end for breakfast. Some groups of families/older travellers were moving slower and will probably take 3-4 hours.Other than worlds end there is "little worlds end", which is exactly what you'd expect, a waterfall which is worth a look, and a walk through pleasant rolling jungle and the plains. The paths aren't perfectly finished and can be uneven for quite long distances, but they're obvious to follow and you won't need a guide.All in all, a good half day.
title: A good walk

body: We visit Horton Plains as part of a Sri Lankan Wildlife tour and hiked the circular route taking in mini World's End, World's End and Baker falls. It was an excellent hike over some challenging terrain (narrow rocky river beds downhill). Thankfully we'd read our itinerary notes and were fully prepared with hiking shoes, apparently a number of visitors had not. How they managed the 3 hour walk in flip flops was beyond me!! The views from mini World's End and World's End are spectacular albeit there were a lot of people there. The lack of any safety railing of course was splendid as it did not spoil the view but was a little disconcerting for those of us that aren't keen on really high cliffs! Deer and stags to be seen on the plains, very close up which was lovely. Birds to be heard - not necessarily seen though - did spot some small ground squirrels and a couple of lizards. Toilet facilities interesting at the start of the park - you are definitely open to the elements! Overall a great experience and fantastic walk in the natural environment of this beautiful country.
title: Great Hike

body: It's more than 9km trail that passes through waterfalls, clouds and dense forests. Carrying enough water is the key and don't try to do it at noon or with kids or elderly people. Fees is 3k lkr for foreigners. It's safe and an amazing experience. Key attractions are waterfall, world's end.
title: Loved it!!! Fitness test

body: Horton Plains National Park is a protected area in the central highlands of Sri Lanka and is covered by montane grassland and cloud forest.
title: Horton Plains National Park

body: Most tours start early from around 5.30am to get up to the plains to avoid the heat . Circuit route best done in a clockwise manner. Cool rock formations , water features, and two stunning viewpoints . Takes around three hours and you need sturdy shoes and maybe waterproofs just in case. Excellent walk and one of the unmissables in Sri Lanka
title: Great way to work off breakfast

body: The forest really gives a sense of what a tropical jungle is. The other half of the trail is in vast vallies with amazing scenic views. Not too hard, around a 7.5 km.The only downside is the early rise.
title: Great views and a nice walk

body: Apparently, everyone includes this on their trip to Sri Lanka! Trekkers, birders, tourists. I couldn't understand why we were being overtaken by jeeps, tuc tucs, bikes, buses at 5.45 am.Only as we neared the entrance did we realise what was going on. It was like Piccadilly Circus in the rush hour only worse. Our jeep was packed in with every other mode of transport and we had to wait for about an hour or longer for our guide to collect a ticket from the ONE booth that was open. Absolute chaos.Even when we eventually got into the park having eaten our packed breakfast from the hotel, there was no organised car parking at the other end so I can't say that I particularly enjoyed the experience. We walked along the tracks as we were birding but even then you had to ensure you weren't wiped out by the jeeps steaming along. Unless you're going for the trekking then I wouldn't bother!
title: Chaotic entry system

body: The walk was superb and great fun, although you need a reasonable level of fitness and (suggest) sensible footwear as the path can be a bit undulating and uneven in places. Total cost for 2, including the car was just short of 7000 Rupees but remember you need to add the cost of whatever form of transport you use to get to the Plains. It’s a long way by car from Nuwara Eliya - c 1.5 hours on a bumpy road each way but well worth it for the view from Worlds End. Aim to get there as early as possible eg be at the start of the Plains walk by 7 am to try to avoid the crowds - many of which simply meander and moan about the terrain. The view when you get to Worlds End is inspiring, but make sure you are at the edge by 1000 hrs as the rain forest clouds quickly rises up from the valley below and covers everything in a moist haze. Plan carefully and leave early and you will have a fantastic experience
title: Get There Early To Avoid Crowds And See The View

body: This is a lovely National Park set in the mountains. Great walks.. Great Views. Good Birding. Lovely vegetation
title: Stunning views rom this really lovely National Park

body: Horton Plains National park is located in the hill country of Sri Lanka. It is not very accessible as the roads are narrow and steep. A payment has to be made to visit the park and the price for 2 adults at the local rate wa approx. Rs. 600. When we visited the customer service centre on the premises we were informed that we should pay the rate for foreigners which was Rs. 3000 each, although we were born in Sri Lanka and spoke the national language fluently. The women at this centre were extremely aggressive and threatened to take us to court if we did not pay this grossly over-priced rate. The entire conversation took place in Fluent Sinhalese and we showed them our place of birth as Colombo, Sri Lanka on our Australian passports. One of the women even attempted to snatch the passports away from us. We therefore reluctantly paid the higher rate, after further argument, for the sake of peace. The males at this centre were quite amenable and were in agreement with us rather than the women. We strongly believe that this money found its way into their pockets.
title: Sadly over-priced

body: We went on the hike, as many people do, early in the morning (6.30). We walked the whole circuit. There were a huge queue of minibuses at the ticket entrance. They are strict on what can be taken onto the plain, so don’t take plastic bags (bottles are fine but they strip off their plastic wrapper) as they will be confiscated during your bag search at the entrance to the walk. If the sun comes out you will need sunscreen as the sun is strong at altitude. We did not see any toilets at the visitor's centre or car park.You will need sturdy trainers and water. You can do the walk in around 3 hours, more if you like to stop to admire the scenery and take photos. Not all the route is an easy path, eg. some boulders to climb over, but we are not big trekkers and found it manageable.There is a waterfall (Baker's Falls), quite a difficult but short climb up to it. If you take the right hand path first on your walk you will do this near the beginning or if you take the left hand path first you will do this ear the end if you do a circular route.We didn’t see any monkeys but heard their calls on a couple of occasions. We saw a few birds, not as many as expected, and a colourful lizard.
title: A lovely walk, but hard work

body: It's wonderful to visit to visitors. We enjoyed. Who ever visit in nuwara eliya.must needs to go this place
title: Super

body: We started very early in the morning, whats necessary, due to the fog coming around 10. The round tour needs about 3hours. Hiking shoes or other stable shoes are necessary, because of partially rocky ground.The nature and landscape is unique. I wish the hiking trail would be longer:) Because of the fact that there is only the one way around it can be crowded on some places. It can be reduced, but I dont want to tell how;)
title: Impressive landscape in the highlands

body: the Horton Plains National Park is simply stunning. The 10km round trip hike, including the Worlds End lookout point took us about 3 hours with lots of stops along the way. Beautiful scenery and wildlife.The path was quite rough in parts and definitely not suitable for those with mobility issues
title: a must do in sri lanka

body: We were advised to start the walk as early as possible I.e. sunrise around 6.30am in order to see the mini and end of the world viewpoints before it is hidden in the clouds. However we only started the trek at 9.30am but we were so lucky. We took the clockwise route, going to mini world first, end of world second and the waterfalls last.We actually saw both end of the worlds just in time, with literally minutes spare before the cloud obliterated everything.Take water with you, good walking boots as it can be slippery in places after rain. There are some rocky patches to go through but although it can be strenuous at times, it is not that difficult.Also by going early you avoid the higher temperatures later in the day.From the first junction, we took 3 hours and it was a really enjoyable trek.It is well marked, and if in this area this is one excursion not to be missed.
title: A great 3 hour hike, but get there early

body: We left at 5.15 am for Horton Plains and weren't disappointed with our 5 mile hike to Worlds End and Baker's Falls. If you don't like walking, don't bother though, as it's quite rough going for a short walk.
title: Well worth the early start

body: My favourite place in Sri Lanka! We hiked to worlds end, a very enjoyable walk (so nice after Adams peak the day before!!). Beautiful views, beautiful park, well worth the visit.
title: Out of this World!!!

body: We went to Horton Plains wanting to take a hike. I was aware it wouldn't be a real hike (boots, stones, steep ground) but actually we didn't feel at all the difference of altitude. It was like a walk in a different park. The most interesting thing is that you can feel the big difference of temperature and moist when you go from the plains into the forest, and vice versa. We got up on World's End when the mist already was there, but the view was amazing!
title: Nice walk

body: The Rough Guide to Sri Lanka describes this hike as "walking in a few gentle hours".This description is highly misleading: The walk is 9 km, some of it climbing, some on rough trails that are closer to dry river beds, where one steps from rock to rock. The hike took me about three and a half hours, and I was exhausted at the end, especially as the climb down, then back up from Baker's Falls, is in the final third of the walk. The scenery is very beautiful, and at World's End utterly gorgeous, though there are few animals to be seen, except for several Samba deer in the parking lot! Even the drive up to the park, in the early morning, with the hills and trees tops poking through the clouds, is beautiful. However, words of warning: pack lots of water, and additional provisions to the breakfast your hotel would have given you - you will need to nourish yourself during the trek. And consider your level of fitness: I saw a lot of exhausted looking older people.
title: A beautiful trek, but demanding

body: Fabulous visit and by leaving at 6 we got pretty good views. The rock strata in the path are amazing - never seen any like them before. Some exhilarating climbs but nothing too challenging (unless you don't like heights!)
title: Exhilarating and magnificent

body: We got up at 4.30 a.m. to go from Nuwara Eliya and it takes about 1hr 25 mins to get there. Crazy queues at entrance though our driver got us through fairly quickly. Very little wildlife, view is OK but photos are difficult because of haze even on a clear morning. Longish walk, about 3 hours. We paid a total price of $100 for driver, park fees etc. Definitely not worth going for the price. We've been in Sri Lanka for 3 weeks and I am just so sick of the way the locals try to rip you off the whole time. You cannot trust anyone. I have travelled all over the world and to much of Asia, Vietnam, Cambodia, Lao, Thailand etc but I have never been anywhere with such dishonest people. They will smile and smile and welcome you etc etc but the first chance they get they will rip you off/overcharge etc. We wish we hadn't come for so long because it has really distorted our view of human nature. As an early explorer once wrote of Sri Lanka: " A paradise island inhabited by devils."
title: Not worth it.

body: one of the most beautiful places i have ever visited in Sri Lanka its totally worth it great views , amazing walk , totally worth it , i can't describe it enough!
title: a must do !

body: We came here as part of our tour of SL without realising it was a 9km walk/hike - some over uneven ground - so being older & one of us with asthma, we could not do the hike.We went for a short walk and it was quite foggy - drifting in and out so views were not great. Talking to other tourists, this was a problem all the way around the walk.
title: Need to be reasonably fit
A good hike around the Plains!!
body: An early start to this place is important weather and temperature wise. The hike takes you on a circular path through the plains and the view of the countryside is beautiful. The vegetation is unique and you get to see many rare highland birds. A good hike and worth it too.

title: Nice walk
body: Walk is nice to get to world’s end particularly if you go their in the early morning.We didn’t find world’s end point of view was incredible.Prices are very high

title: You could almost be in the UK!
body: This was a most enjoyable circular walk although the terrain and weather (it started off being cool and damp but brightened up to be like an early summer's day in the UK) rather reminded me of Shropshire!We didn't go early but in some respects that was no bad thing as we met people who had had to wait ages to get a ticket. We still had a bit of a wait but I would have been more bothered if I'd got up early.It was quite busy especially at World's End full of people taking the inevitable selfies. The walk is a bit more than moderate with lots of up and down, some steps, some rocks. Trainers were fine and I noticed people in all sorts of strange footwear who still managed to do the circuit. I wish I'd worn gym leggings rather than baggy trousers.Nice to get a bit of exercise, not always easy on holiday.

title: Another world
body: The circular walk that most people follow takes in a range of terrains, and it can be rough underfoot: good walking shoes are an advantage here. Take a few hours to enjoy the scenery. I reached World's End after the mist had rolled in so I didn't get to see the spectacular views; though I was enchanted by the cloud forest which is the natural alternative. Definitely worth the effort to visit this place, though don't expect to be alone - it's popular.

title: A Marvelous Stroll
body: The day and time came perfect, with a light shower of drizzle and mist intermittently, giving it the right balance of coolness, the foggy outfit and the adventurous feeling that you are seeing the unseen. The landscape was out of the world and the staff managing the entrance were helpful and cordial.

title: Make sure you go very early in the morning
body: The park gate opens at 7am but there is a one hour long que to buy tickets at the entrance. The last 2 km of the road is in really bad shape so expect a bumpy ride. Make sure you reach the ticket counter as early as possible. Its a long hike on the open terrace from the gate. Take drinking water and wear hiking cloths. Toilets are a bit unclean.Unrealistic ticket prices for foreigners. Main attraction is scenery and sambar deer.

title: Loved the veiw
body: Loved the views from the Worlds end. Although the views may not be mesmerizing its still nice to see the vast expansion of greenery in Sri Lanka.

title: Amazing hike!!!
body: So much to see from the incredible trees to the bright pink rocks but most importantly the incredible sights of the waterfall and world’s end! The breathtaking views were so worth the hike! The water was too cold to take a dip but we carefully went down some rocks to the bottom of the waterfall and it was really incredible and a very refreshing moment on the hike. Our guide said to plan 3-4 hours to complete the entire hike but we moved rather quickly as a group and finished in under 3 hours.

title: Beautiful and chilly
body: Went early in the morning to a nice ~9km hike. Beautiful scenery and with luck you might see some wildlife too. Weather is unpredictable. Started a raincoat on, walked with my t-shirt on for a while and after the smaller world's end had to put my coat back on. Remember, no plastic allowed to the park (except water bottle).

title: Nice park for a walk
body: Lovely views from Worlds End and in general. The queue at the entrance was extremely long - for the entrance money people pay there should be more attendants issuing tickets.
